feature.name: Authorizations and Authentications
feature.description: The feature defines the complete requirements for human Authorizations and Authentications that use '{env}.chathealthy.ai' and chathealthy.ai. The scope of this excludes how users in the Dev Ops pipelines and processes manage their entitlements and identities.

story.name: GUID — stable per-session auth credential
story.description: The stable 32-char session identifier carried inside the security token. Manufactured once per page session and preserved across every cross-service hop.

requirement.requirement: The session token MUST use a stable GUID that identifies the session for its lifetime. The GUID MUST NOT change between calls within the same session.
requirement.name: GUID is stable across all inter-service calls in a session

requirement.requirement: The GUID MUST be 16 bytes (128 bits) generated by the UUID version 4 algorithm (RFC 4122), rendered as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters with no separators.
requirement.name: GUID is 16 bytes

story.name: NONCE — fresh-per-hop replay defense
story.description: The 17-char timestamp stamped freshly by every server on receive. Defends against replay per NIST 800-53 SC-23. Distinct from the GUID; only the nonce changes per hop.

requirement.requirement: The nonce (timestamps) MUST be regenerated fresh on every inter-service call. The nonce MUST NOT be reused across calls. Every ChatHealthy component (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) that receives a token MUST update the last_used timestamp in the nonce to prove it processed the token at that time. Reusing a nonce is a replay attack vector and fails NIST 800-53 SC-23 (Session Authenticity).
requirement.name: Nonce regenerated fresh per hop and stamped by every receiving service

requirement.requirement: But the value of the NONCE will be updated correctly with the new time where it belongs, in the right panel if ownership is passed to EvaluateCare or Shared Services, and in the Left Panel if control is passed to FindCare. Only the owning service Shall update the NONCE.
requirement.name: Only the owning service updates the displayed nonce; updated panel is the one that owns the page

requirement.requirement: The nonce field MUST be 35 bytes in the exact TimeByteOrder YYYYMMDDHHMMSSmmmXYYYYMMDDHHMMSSmmm - two UTC wall-clock timestamps in YYYYMMDDHHMMSSmmm format (17 bytes each: year 4, month 2, day 2, hour 2, minute 2, second 2, millisecond 3 bytes; ASCII digits, no separators) separated by a single literal uppercase ASCII 'X' pad character at byte position 18. The first 17 bytes are the original mint time; the pad 'X' is byte 18; the next 17 bytes are the most-recent restamp time.
requirement.name: Nonce is 35 bytes

requirement.requirement: Bytes 1-17 of the nonce field hold the original mint timestamp. Bytes 19-35 hold the most-recent restamp timestamp. Both values are identical at mint; the latter advances on each restamp while the former is preserved.
requirement.name: Nonce byte order: original 1-17, latest 19-35

story.name: Security Token — signed wire envelope
story.description: The wire object and its content exchanged between services: { origin, token (CH{nonce}{created}{guid}), signature, created_at, signed, server_env }. Binds the GUID and nonce under an RSA PKCS1v15 SHA256 signature by the current stamping origin.

requirement.requirement: Every session token generated by a ChatHealthy service MUST include an `origin` field whose value is the name of the originating service (FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices). The token's signature MUST be produced with that service's own private key. Any service receiving a token MUST verify the signature using the named origin's public certificate and MUST reject the token if the origin field does not match the signing key. The session token display — both the left panel at creation and the right panel after a cross-service handoff — MUST render the origin value as a labeled field so a human can visually confirm which service signed the token.
requirement.name: Session token must include and display service origin, signed and verified per-service

requirement.requirement: The session_token.origin field returned by /verify-token (and any equivalent endpoint that returns a session_token object) MUST be set to the name of the RESPONDING service (e.g., "EvaluateCare" for EvaluateCare's /verify-token; "SharedServices" for SharedServices'). This origin field is the SELF-IDENTIFICATION of the service that produced THIS response object — it is distinct from the cryptographic token signer (REQ-017, which always identifies FindCare). One service MUST NOT assert another service's identity in any field rendered to the operator. The wrapper's session-verification panel MUST render this origin value as-is, treating it as the responding service's authoritative claim of its own identity. The display proves that the named component received and updated the nonce and token and produced this verification result.
requirement.name: verify-token response origin field self-identifies the responding service

requirement.requirement: Session token mutual authentication MUST pass for SharedServices. The same token FindCare created MUST be the same one SharedServices received.
requirement.name: Enforce SharedServices mutual auth using FindCare-created session token

requirement.requirement: Any call from FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices to one another MUST complete a mutual-authentication TLS 1.2+ handshake. A failed or incomplete handshake is a fatal error per EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-B-002.
requirement.name: Mutual-authentication TLS 1.2+ for FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices inter-service calls

requirement.requirement: For non-production environments (local, dev, qa), if session-token verification or mutual-authentication handshake (per EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-T-003) fails to complete or does not return a definitive VERIFIED/FAILED result within 30 seconds, the state is illegal. The UI MUST render a 'Fatal Error' splash in the center panel and display Verified: FAILED in the session verification panel. The UI MUST NOT display 'Pending' for longer than 30 seconds. In production, any runtime security-primitive failure MUST cause the hard process exit defined in EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-T-004.
requirement.name: Render Fatal Error splash if session authentication fails or times out in non-prod

requirement.requirement: On startup every server MUST exercise each security primitive it uses (session-token generation, signature signing and verification, credential redaction, mTLS handshake, key decryption, authentication check). If any exercise fails the process MUST exit with a non-zero code. A server MUST NOT serve any request after a failed startup exercise. Exit codes: 78 (configuration failure — missing library, missing cert, missing env var, malformed primitive output), 77 (permission denied on cert or key file), 70 (unexpected internal error). Stderr MUST name the primitive that failed.
requirement.name: Startup must test security primitives; exit on failure with specific codes

requirement.requirement: When the user transfers page ownership to EvaluateCare or SharedServices, the right-panel mutual-authentication request (/verify-token) MUST be issued by the browser directly to the cold-button service (the new owner) and MUST NOT be proxied through FindCare. The browser MUST use the cold service's environment-specific URL (HF Space URL for dev/qa/prod, https://localhost:PORT for local) as the request target. The cold service's /verify-token response — including the verified session token — MUST be the source of the data rendered in the right panel. This ensures the right panel reflects the actual active service's verification, not FindCare's proxied view of it, and is independently verifiable by inspecting the browser DevTools Network tab. CORS on EvaluateCare and SharedServices MUST allow the wrapper origins (localhost, dev.chathealthy.ai, qa.chathealthy.ai, chathealthy.ai). The /session call (token issuance) MUST target the originating service per EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-T-001 (origin field signed with that service's private key). Verification: Code/deploy/localSmokeTestPyTest.py and Code/deploy/devSmokeTestPyTest.py TestStep25.test_push_shared_services MUST register a network listener before the SharedServices banner button click and assert (a) at least one POST to SHARED_URL+'/verify-token' (direct call) and (b) zero POSTs ending in '/shared/verify-token' (no proxy). See BUG-VERIFY-TOKEN-PROXY-001.
requirement.name: Browser must call cold-button service directly for verify-token (no FindCare proxy)

requirement.requirement: GET /session must return a signed session token with origin=FindCare. Falls back to unsigned token if cert unavailable.
requirement.name: GET /session returns signed token with origin=FindCare; fallback to unsigned if cert unavailable

requirement.requirement: The session token display MUST separate the nonce from the GUID so a human can visually verify each part. The display MUST show: (1) Signed token (the encrypted signature), (2) Nonce (the two timestamps extracted from the token), (3) GUID (the session identifier extracted from the token). The nonce and GUID MUST be displayed as separate labeled fields. The presentation in the right panel (after EvaluateCare or SharedServices handoff) MUST be identical to the presentation in the left panel. Both panels MUST use the same labels, layout, and format.
requirement.name: Signed-token panel renders signed token, nonce, GUID as separate labeled fields, identical in both panels

requirement.requirement: All traffic MUST be HTTPS with mutual authentication.
requirement.name: All inter-service traffic uses mutual authentication over HTTPS

requirement.requirement: MUST comply with EPIC-002-F-003-S-001-REQ-T-002.
requirement.name: Comply with the GUID specification

requirement.requirement: The session-verification widget MUST display the time in UTC.
requirement.name: Time displayed in UTC
Session token byte assembly: GUID, first timestamp, X, second timestamp
requirement.requirement: The session token MUST be assembled in exactly this byte order: (1) the 32-character GUID per EPIC-002-F-003-S-001-REQ-T-002; (2) immediately followed by the 17-byte first timestamp; (3) immediately followed by a single literal uppercase ASCII 'X' character; (4) immediately followed by the 17-byte second timestamp. The two timestamps and their semantics are defined by EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-T-001, EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-T-002, and EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-B-002.

story.description: ChatHealthy.ai MUST support the creation and use of identity-provider IDs (Google, Facebook, Apple, and others as introduced) for logins using each identity provider's OAuth capabilities. The firm and its application rely on identity providers as identity sources. This story specifies all the technical and business requirements for this capability.

requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy.ai MUST support the creation and use of identity-provider IDs (Google, Facebook, Apple, and others as introduced) for logins using each identity provider's OAuth capabilities. The firm and its application rely on identity providers as identity sources. This story specifies all the technical and business requirements for this capability.

requirement.name: Playwright test of the Login & Registration sequence of screens and messages

requirement.name: Login & Registration link in the static-site navigation
requirement.requirement: Every static page on the chathealthy.ai website MUST render a top-level navigation with exactly three links, in this left-to-right order: Home, Login & Registration, Products and Services.

requirement.name: Login click signals login_register intent and identity_provider to /gate
requirement.requirement: On a click of the Login & Registration link, the browser MUST POST to the SharedServices /gate endpoint with the request body carrying intent = "login_register" and an identity_provider field set to the operator-selected identity provider.

requirement.name: AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.run() routes to utterance or to a control use case
requirement.requirement: AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.run() MUST route each request into exactly one of two top-level paths: (a) the utterance path, or (b) the control path. Requests on the control path MUST identify a single control use case (for example, login_register) and MUST invoke the corresponding tool or process. An unrecognized path or an unknown control use case MUST cause a hard error.

requirement.name: login_register intent triggers OAuth at the selected identity provider
requirement.requirement: When AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.run() observes intent = "login_register", it MUST return a Response whose redirect_url field is the SharedServices /auth/<identity_provider>/start endpoint URL for the identity provider carried in the request.

requirement.name: /gate emits redirect event when AuthN returns redirect_url
requirement.requirement: When the AuthN Response carries a non-null redirect_url, the SharedServices /gate route MUST emit, as the terminal NDJSON event, a record of the shape {"type": "redirect", "url": <redirect_url>} and end the response.

requirement.name: Frontend follows redirect events
requirement.requirement: On any /gate NDJSON event of shape {"type": "redirect", "url": <string>}, the frontend consumer MUST call window.location.assign(<url>).

requirement.name: /auth/<identity_provider>/callback exchanges the authorization code
requirement.requirement: The SharedServices /auth/<identity_provider>/callback endpoint MUST receive the identity provider's authorization-code redirect, exchange the code with the identity provider's token endpoint, and obtain the identity provider's stable identifier (hereafter the identity-provider user ID) and the verified email claim.

requirement.name: Users collection stores user_objects, indexed on lookup keys
requirement.requirement: Each document in the users collection IS a UserObject conforming to the canonical schema at https://dev.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyUserStateSchema.json. The collection MUST maintain a unique index on user_id and multi-key indexes on OAuthIdentities.identity_provider_user_id and on OAuthIdentities.email so the OAuth callback can perform constant-time lookups.

requirement.name: Registration creates the users record
requirement.requirement: When no existing users record carries { identity_provider: <identity provider>, identity_provider_user_id: <identity-provider user ID> } in its OAuthIdentities AND no existing OAuthIdentities[].email matches the verified email returned by this callback, the SharedServices /auth/<identity_provider>/callback endpoint MUST create a new users record (a UserObject) with: user_id set to a freshly generated random GUID (RFC 4122 UUIDv4); OAuthIdentities set to exactly one entry { identity_provider: <identity provider>, identity_provider_user_id: <identity-provider user ID>, email: <identity-provider email> }; public_username set to the verified email returned by the identity provider (this default value may be changed by the user via a future story); is_registered = True; user_type = "Prospect".

requirement.name: Persist mirrors user_object to the users collection when is_registered == True
requirement.requirement: AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.persist() MUST, on every invocation, write the current user_object to admin.sessions (keyed by GUID). When the user_object's is_registered == True, persist() MUST ALSO write the same user_object to the users collection (keyed by user_id). The two writes MUST carry the same UserObject value.

requirement.name: Returning OAuth login replaces the guest user_object with the DB user_object
requirement.requirement: On a successful OAuth callback whose OAuthIdentities lookup matches an existing user's { identity_provider, identity_provider_user_id }, the endpoint MUST reuse that record's existing user_id, MUST refresh that entry's email to the email returned by the identity provider on this callback, MUST re-set ChatHealthyRegisteredUserCookie per EPIC-002-F-003-S-006-REQ-T-004, MUST replace the current session's guest user_object with the stored UserObject, and MUST bind that stored UserObject to the current session.

requirement.name: UserObject defines OAuthIdentities, an array of identity-provider identities
requirement.requirement: The UserObject schema MUST define a field named OAuthIdentities of type array. Each array element MUST be an object with exactly three sub-fields: (a) identity_provider - the identity-provider name; the enum is open and includes each supported identity provider (initially "Google", with additional identity providers added as introduced); (b) identity_provider_user_id - the identity provider's stable identifier for the user; (c) email - the verified email returned by the identity provider on its most recent OAuth callback for this user. The array MUST be non-empty whenever is_registered == True.

requirement.name: Returning login appends the guest conversation onto the stored user history
requirement.requirement: On a successful OAuth callback handled by EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-012, before the stored UserObject replaces the current session's guest UserObject, the endpoint MUST append the guest UserObject's session_conversation_history.utterances, session_conversation_history.ux_events, and session_conversation_history.unanswered_questions arrays to the corresponding arrays of the stored UserObject's session_conversation_history. The merged UserObject (stored history first, then the appended guest entries) MUST then be written to the users collection and bound to the current session.

requirement.name: Cross-identity-provider reconciliation via verified email
requirement.requirement: On every successful OAuth callback, the endpoint MUST first attempt to match (identity_provider, identity_provider_user_id) against any user_object.OAuthIdentities entry across the users collection. When that match succeeds, the returning-login path per EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-012 runs. Otherwise, the endpoint MUST attempt to match the verified email returned by this callback against any user_object.OAuthIdentities[].email. When that match succeeds, the endpoint MUST append { identity_provider, identity_provider_user_id, email } to that user's OAuthIdentities, re-set ChatHealthyRegisteredUserCookie per EPIC-002-F-003-S-006-REQ-T-004 with that user's existing user_id, replace the current session's guest user_object with the stored UserObject, and bind that stored UserObject to the current session. Otherwise, the registration path per EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-009 runs.

ch_session carries the session token; server surfaces time_remaining; client tracks it and pre-flights
requirement.requirement: Every SharedServices /gate response MUST (a) set a Secure, HttpOnly cookie named ch_session with Max-Age=300 whose value is the session token defined by EPIC-002-F-003-S-003-REQ-B-007, and (b) include in the response body a field named time_remaining_seconds whose integer value is the seconds remaining between the moment of response and the most-recent-restamp timestamp (bytes 19-35 of the nonce per EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-B-002) plus the 300-second TTL. The browser MUST store the most-recent time_remaining_seconds together with the local clock value at receipt, and MUST update that stored pair on every subsequent /gate response. Before issuing any SharedServices request the browser MUST compute the remaining time from that stored pair against its local clock and refuse to issue the request when the remaining time has elapsed. All browser-side reads and writes of any ChatHealthy.ai cookie MUST be performed by exactly one shared JavaScript file (served with Content-Type text/javascript) loaded by index.html; no other browser code, including inline scripts within index.html, may read or write any ChatHealthy.ai cookie.

requirement.name: /gate response body includes time_remaining_seconds

requirement.name: time_remaining_seconds value is computed from the nonce restamp
requirement.requirement: time_remaining_seconds MUST equal (most_recent_restamp_timestamp + 300 seconds) - server_response_instant, computed in UTC milliseconds and floored to whole seconds, where most_recent_restamp_timestamp is bytes 19-35 of the nonce per EPIC-002-F-003-S-002-REQ-B-002.

requirement.name: Browser pre-flights every SharedServices request against the stored pair
requirement.requirement: Before issuing any SharedServices request the browser MUST compute remaining = stored_time_remaining_seconds - (Date.now() - stored_receipt_clock) / 1000, and MUST refuse to issue the request when remaining <= 0.

feature.name: Universal Navigation
feature.description: The ChatHealthy.ai application guides users to find care, evaluate their choices objectively, and meet with their loved ones, care providers, and AI robots to discuss their options, and potentially get deep research based on their context. Users might be registered, guests, customers, or site administrators. The requirements for One Universal Navigation Mechanism are specified herein. Navigation takes place between an end user typing values into a prompt or using one of ChatHealthy's tools and corresponding UX component to do work such as picking providers, specialties, clinical trials, or tuning the mixing board in EvaluateCare. These requirements when met must, along with other controls, demonstrate ChatHealthy's compliance with NIST 800-53. I.e., they must meet the strictest requirements that any HIPAA audit might uncover.

Every browser-initiated HTTP call from any ChatHealthy.ai surface - the wrapper site, embedded FindCare/EvaluateCare iframes, future mobile webviews, future native clients - funnels through this one endpoint. SharedServices performs any cross-component work server-to-server on behalf of the client.

Other calls to other URLs, except for the domain name by itself, MUST result in a 404; i.e., calls to http://chathealthy.ai, https://chathealthy.ai, http://dev.chathealthy.ai, https://dev.chathealthy.ai, http://qa.chathealthy.ai, https://qa.chathealthy.ai MUST all redirect to the universal gate call.

Downstream tools register with the router at build time, supplying their TOOL_NAME, Request schema, and natural-language minimum/total requirement strings per entity. The router MUST expose a metadata API by which any caller can retrieve, at runtime, either the full registry OR a single tool's metadata by TOOL_NAME. Build-time registration; runtime read-only access. The registry is the single source of truth for tool addressability.

requirement.name: Registration entries carry per-attribute natural-language requirement statements

feature.name: Utterance Tool
feature.description: This feature defines the requirement for the handling of every utterance made by users of ChatHealthy.ai's core front end application. All utterances have 2 possible paths: 1- they either invoke a response that asks the user directly or indirectly questions that will help it either get to know the user better, or route the user to an appropriate tool. 2 - Based on the utterance the intent of the user seems clear and a tool is invoked that will allow data to be passed back to the front end and displayed. An utterance is the words that a user either types into a prompt into the UX or otherwise uses natural language to tell the application about themselves and what they want. This feature will not be complete until the entire application's code base utilizes this architecture of tool to Front end intermediated by utterance.

story.name: Universal utterance routing
story.description: The single canonical routing path for every user utterance from the input control through to the terminal user_object update. Holds the business rule that all utterances flow through this path and the technical contract for each hop in the path.

requirement.name: All user utterances must flow through the user-prompt tool
requirement.requirement: Every user prompt coming from any component, e.g. user-prompt input, where a user uses natural language to communicate with the app MUST flow through the UniversalNavigationTool to the UtteranceManager.

requirement.name: User object is the tool's input
requirement.requirement: The tool's input MUST be a User State object as canonically defined by EPIC-002-F-003 (Authorizations and Authentications).

depends_on.reason: Defines the canonical User State / User Object

requirement.name: Tool must be tightly coupled with a front end component
requirement.requirement: The tool MUST be tightly coupled with a front-end JS file that: (1) takes the input from the user and sends it to the universal router using the universal router's input pydantic tool as a JSON; if and only if the router determines that it was an utterance shall the router construct the pydantic object and pass it to the tool. The component MUST be capable of both transmitting the user's input and responding in text if further natural language input is required from the user.

depends_on.reason: Universal Navigation feature — defines the universal router

requirement.name: UtteranceManager obtains tool metadata from the router and caches it at runtime
requirement.requirement: UtteranceManager MUST obtain downstream-tool metadata from the universal router's metadata API per EPIC-002-F-004-S-002-REQ-B-001. UtteranceManager MUST cache the retrieved metadata at runtime — the API call is for cache population on startup (or on cache invalidation), not a per-utterance lookup. The router's registry is the source of truth; UtteranceManager holds a runtime copy.

depends_on.reason: Defines the router-side registry and metadata API that UtteranceManager caches

requirement.name: Universal utterance tool must be capable of doing multi-thread processing
requirement.requirement: The universal utterance tool must be capable of multi-threaded processing. It might make parallel calls to Mongo, and/or LLMs. Within that multithreaded environment, if required and one thread with precedence returns, the tool must be capable of calling on a tool prior to the other tools completing their activities.

requirement.name: Universal utterance round-trip path
requirement.requirement: Every utterance MUST complete the full round-trip path. Outbound: (1) user input enters at the user-prompt input; (2) front-end JS routes the utterance from client to server; (3) the universal router receives it on the server side; (4) the router constructs the User-object payload and dispatches to UtteranceManager; (5) UtteranceManager classifies and returns a decision: exactly one of two outcomes — (a) the name of a downstream registered tool to invoke (the safety tool, FindCare, EvaluateCare, or any other registered tool), or (b) a clarifying-question / feedback-request message to send back to the user; (6) on outcome (a), the universal router invokes the named downstream tool with the User-object payload. Inbound: (7) the resolved response — tool data or clarifying message — flows back through the universal router; (8) the router routes the response from server to the originating client; (9) the front-end JS receives it and renders to the user, completing the loop. No utterance may bypass UtteranceManager. UtteranceManager MUST NOT invoke downstream tools itself — only the universal router does. Every utterance MUST produce a delivered response.

feature.name: Specialty Filter
feature.description: Filter search results by specialty type, prescriber status, and homeopathic status. The term 'Homeopathic' in this feature refers to a Homeopathic provider — it is not a new classification and is not an umbrella label for the broader CAM/holistic/integrative-medicine set. Six-story decomposition: Display Specification, Present Initial Filter, User Manages Filter, User Submits Filter, API Surface and Contracts, Test Coverage.

story.description: How the SpecialtyFilter LOOKS and behaves end-to-end as a panel. Anchors the comprehensive UX description that S-002, S-003, and S-004 reference.

requirement.requirement:
The header uses a light green background. {find actual coded RGB value, or the term the CSS style sheet uses}
It is divided into three rows: a title row, a 'count' row, and a 'controls' row.
The title row says 'Choose Specialties'.
The Count row has 3 values where the label for each value is over the actual value. From left to right, the three values are:
"All possible": composed of the count of all the specialty types that can give care to the user based on the question they asked. This is regardless of whether or not a provider is available within the geographic boundary established by the user's question. In this group a specialty type must have a license but might not be homeopathic, or be able to prescribe.
"All prescribers": the total number of specialty types from 'All possible' that are legally allowed to write prescriptions. This includes, for example, Nurse Practitioners, and is not limited to physicians.
"Your choices": all the specialty types that the user has chosen. They might for example click the uncheck button and then check three specialties; in that case the number would be 3.
Macro Controls
The third row has three controls: a button 'Uncheck all' and two checkboxes 'Prescribers' and 'Homeopathic'. The two checkboxes are stacked vertically whereas the Uncheck button takes up the entire vertical space in this row. The controls in this header row do NOT determine what is submitted when Apply Filter is clicked — the only criterion for what gets submitted is the list of checked specialties. The header controls affect that checked-list state, but their purpose is to control which specialties are checked or presented; they are not intended to control what is done when Apply Filter is applied. The behavior of these controls is:
Uncheck All
"Uncheck all": this button unchecks any specialty type that is checked. Each time it is clicked it does this. If there are no specialties checked this button is greyed out, and a tool tip says, 'No specialties are checked'.
Additional requirement
When fewer than 50% of the rows are unchecked, the button's label reads 'Check All'. When it is in this state, the action is to check all specialties.
Prescribers
The list of checked specialists will have a particular state prior to the user clicking the Prescribers checkbox.
For all prescribers, Homeopathic and others, if the checkbox is unchecked it gets checked. If it is checked it remains checked.
For all non-prescribers, Homeopathic and non-Homeopath, if their checkbox is unchecked or checked, after this box is checked, the box becomes unchecked.
Homeopathic
The list of checked specialists will have a particular state prior to the user clicking the 'Homeopathic' checkbox.
For all Homeopathic specialties that treat this disorder specifically, if their checkbox is unchecked it gets checked. If it is checked it remains checked.
For all non-Homeopathic, prescribers or non-prescribers, if their checkbox is unchecked or checked, after this box is checked, the box becomes unchecked.
Additional behavior:
The result set returned to this list upon initialization will have two lists.
List one includes Homeopath specialties that specifically treat the class of problem that the user presented to the engine.
List two includes all homeopathic specialties in this area or generalists that can treat this type of problem. The server will try to eliminate non-logical choices such as midwives to treat erectile dysfunction or gerontologists to treat a child.
From a UX perspective there is only one list.
Scrollbar behavior
If there are more than 10 (configurable) then they are in a scroll bar, but all are available if the user scrolls.
Each specialty has on its right a checkbox. By default, all are checked. A user can check or uncheck any specialty. And they can click the Uncheck all button to remove all from being checked. This is going to be a typical behavior; user unchecks all and then checks some.
"Apply Filter" button: at the bottom of the control is a button labeled 'Apply Filter'. The scope of what gets applied is the specific specialties that are checked from the list of specialties. What is done with the controls in the header is not relevant to what specialties are submitted. Their purpose is to control which are checked or presented. They are not intended to control what is done when Apply Filter is applied. If any changes to the list of checked specialties have been made, then when this button is clicked:
A list of providers (the default list) will be in the center panel. Below that, potentially some providers might have been selected.
The provider list subject to selection but not selected shall be turned 'white' i.e. no records shall show.
A timer identical to the one that accompanied the original search shall be presented.
The selected provider window shall remain as is.
The prompt shall be available to the user.
The timer next to the prompt shall also show.
Middle-screen behavior on Apply Filter (per Skip clarification on the 'default list' / preservation question): the entire middle screen MUST be preserved as is from a business perspective. Specifically: the user's question is repainted; the Available Provider list is repainted; the Selected-for-evaluation panel never went away; the Prompt and 'send' never went away. Fine-grained technical requirements may be crafted from this baseline.
Timers (per Skip clarification): there are two timers. One timer is shown immediately to the LEFT of the user-prompt input box. The second timer is on the main screen. The main-screen timer is correct on Apply Filter except that the user's selected providers panel must be preserved (per the middle-screen-behavior clarification above). The prompt-adjacent timer is correct as is.
If no changes to the filter have been made (changes meaning new checks have been made) then the button will not be hot but greyed out, and if a user clicks the button a non-modal popup with an 'OK' button must say: 'There are no changes to apply, try a new prompt if this is the wrong list. The AI agent will help you craft the right question' and no other action will be taken.
Cache Results on client: in order to enhance performance and in contradiction to the general requirement that all business logic must be done in ChatHealthy's servers in the data center, the list of specialists MUST be cached on the client. Each time a new list of specialists is produced by the FindCare server the entire cache content must be replaced with the new list of specialties.

story.name: Rules infrastructure: manager, base worker, lock, timeout, telemetry, exit-code aggregation
story.description: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager + EnforcementWorker (abstract base) deliver the framework: read-only rules-registry load, hook-filtered enforcement dispatch, manager-owned mutex coordination, per-worker subprocess timeout, structured violation/telemetry envelopes, and worst-code-wins aggregation. Per V20 §4.4. The manager is invoked by every Git and Claude Code hook with a single hook_name argument.

requirement.name: Rules carry enforcement entries
requirement.requirement: Every engineering rule that the team intends to enforce MUST carry at least one programmatic enforcement entry. A rule with an empty enforcement array is documentation, not governance, and SHALL be either populated, retired, or annotated as documentation-only.

requirement.name: Enforcement at hook moment
requirement.requirement: Enforcement runs at the moment a violation can occur — the relevant Git or Claude Code hook — not on a separate cadence. There is no nightly job that catches yesterday's mistake.

requirement.name: Hook-agnostic framework
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule MUST be able to attach to any of the four Git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push) and any of the six Claude Code hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded). The framework is hook-agnostic; the enforcement entry declares its hook.

requirement.name: Human debuggability
requirement.requirement: The system MUST be debuggable by a human. One file per role. One class per file. One entry point. Per-enforcement, per-worker structured stdout and telemetry, with worst exit code propagated.

requirement.name: Multi-PID concurrency
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST handle multi-PID race conditions correctly. The same hook can fire many times concurrently across different Claude Code PIDs and Git invocations. The manager acquires a lock before dispatching any worker whose enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True; in-process locks are forbidden.

requirement.name: Additive enforcement
requirement.requirement: Adding the next enforcement MUST be a small, additive change. New enforcement entries get a new enforcement_id and — if needed — a new worker subclass; existing rules and workers are not touched.

requirement.name: Worker inherits base class
requirement.requirement: Every worker MUST inherit from EnforcementWorker. Subclasses implement only their domain-specific check logic. The base class owns scope evaluation, violation shape, exit codes, telemetry, and error handling so every worker behaves the same from the manager's perspective.

requirement.name: Enforcement entry first-class
requirement.requirement: Enforcement entries are first-class records: every entry carries a stable enforcement_id (format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN), a declared hook, an executable_path, a scopes field carrying scope-list rules in the four canonical types (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern), and a requires_lock boolean. They can be cited in audit trails, bug reports, and the backlog like requirements are today.

requirement.name: Filesystem mirrors operating model
requirement.requirement: The architecture MUST be aligned with the EPIC / Feature / Story tree. Filesystem mirrors operating model. The home for this feature is projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/. crossEpicConcerns/ holds shared business artifacts only — no code lives there.

requirement.name: V1 demonstrability
requirement.requirement: Once V1 ships, BR-1 through BR-9 are demonstrably satisfied for the worked example (file scanning on pre-commit) and the framework is in place to absorb every other rule on its own schedule.

requirement.name: Four canonical scope-list types
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST support all four scope-list types on every enforcement entry, even when a given worker uses only a subset. The four permitted terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern) are the only vocabulary used anywhere in this system.

requirement.name: Enforcement schema fields
requirement.requirement: engineering_rules.json schema gains the following required fields per enforcement entry: enforcement_id (string, format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN); hook (enum: pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded); executable_path (string — repo-relative path to the worker script that implements this enforcement); requires_lock (boolean — true if the manager must acquire a lock before dispatching this worker); scopes (array of three-column arrays — [function_name: str, scope_list_type: str, list_of_terms: list[str]] — carrying this enforcement's per-enforcement scope-list rules; scope_list_type ∈ {allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern}; the EngineeringRulesSchema.json validator enforces this row shape; see §4.6); timeout (integer, optional — seconds; defaults to manager constant DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30 when omitted; the manager passes this value to subprocess.run(..., timeout=N); on timeout the manager kills the worker subprocess and returns EXIT_WORKER_TIMEOUT (4); the worker does not see this field — the timeout is enforced by the parent process; see §4.3.2). The four scope-list types are carried only by scopes; there are no separate top-level allowed_exact / allowed_pattern / excluded_exact / excluded_pattern fields on the entry.

requirement.name: Manager class and exit codes
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager lives at projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py. Single class. Single main. Constructor signature __init__(hook_name: str). run returns int. The manager module defines the following named exit-code constants and run returns one of them: EXIT_OK = 0 (all matched enforcements passed), EXIT_VIOLATIONS_FOUND = 1 (at least one worker reported violations; commit/push must block), EXIT_MANAGER_ERROR = 2 (manager-level failure: cannot read engineering_rules.json, malformed schema, unknown hook name, or any other pre-dispatch error), EXIT_WORKER_SPAWN_FAILURE = 3 (one or more workers could not be launched: missing executable_path, executable not found, permission denied, OSError on subprocess), EXIT_WORKER_TIMEOUT = 4 (one or more workers exceeded the configured subprocess timeout), EXIT_WORKER_INTERNAL_ERROR = 5 (a worker exited with a non-0 / non-1 status — i.e. anything ≥ 3 from a worker is treated as an internal worker failure rather than a violation). Aggregation by precedence (highest wins): 2 > 3 > 5 > 4 > 1 > 0. Manager-level errors trump worker errors trump violations trump success, so the caller can immediately tell whether the issue is in the framework or in the user's code. Worker exit codes follow the same convention for the worker's subset: 0 = clean, 1 = violations, 2 = worker error; any worker exit ≥ 3 is promoted by the manager to EXIT_WORKER_INTERNAL_ERROR.

requirement.name: Manager load-filter-spawn
requirement.requirement: Manager loads engineering_rules.json read-only, filters enforcement[] by hook, and for each matching enforcement reads executable_path and spawns the worker via subprocess.run([sys.executable, executable_path, enforcement_id], timeout=...). The manager collects each subprocess returncode and aggregates by the TR-2 exit-code precedence.

requirement.name: EnforcementWorker base class
requirement.requirement: EnforcementWorker (abstract base) lives at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/enforcement_worker.py. It owns: __init__(enforcement_id), _load_enforcement, is_in_scope(resource), main (CLI entry that parses enforcement_id, instantiates the subclass, calls run, returns its exit code), violation emission, telemetry emission, and structured error handling. Subclasses implement run and any private helper methods their domain requires.

requirement.name: Violation record shape
requirement.requirement: Violation record shape (emitted by the base class): {enforcement_id, rule_id, resource, message, severity}. severity in {info, warn, error}.

requirement.name: Telemetry envelope
requirement.requirement: Telemetry envelope (emitted by the base class): start record and end record per worker invocation, both carrying enforcement_id, hook, duration_ms, files_scanned, violation_count, exit_code. Format: one JSON object per line to stdout.

requirement.name: Manager-owned mutex
requirement.requirement: When an enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True, the manager MUST acquire a process-safe lock keyed on enforcement_id before invoking subprocess.run, and MUST release the lock after subprocess.run returns (clean, non-zero, or timeout). Default mechanism: advisory file lock. In-process Python locks are forbidden. Workers do not declare a concurrency primitive.

requirement.name: Manager-worker contract
requirement.requirement: Manager and workers MUST NOT import each other's internals. The only contract is enforcement_id (str) in via CLI argv, exit code (int) out via subprocess returncode, and the structured stdout (violation + telemetry) envelope.

requirement.name: Tests location
requirement.requirement: Tests live at architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/tests/. The base class ships with its own test suite covering scope evaluation, exit-code semantics, violation shape, telemetry envelope, and the try/except fail-safe. Each new worker ships with at least one happy-path and one violation-path test.

requirement.name: Hook plumbing
requirement.requirement: Hook plumbing..git/hooks/{pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push} each invoke `python <repo-root>/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py --hook <hook>`..claude/settings.json registers the same invocation under SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded with the matching `--hook <hook_name>` flag. A pytest under architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/tests/ MUST verify, for every hook named above: (a) hard assert the wire-up exists when the hook carries at least one enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json; (b) advisory warning when the wire-up is missing and the hook has no enforcement (reserved for future Phase-6 workers). The test runs in the F-002 suite and the hard assertions gate pre-push.

requirement.name: Worker taxonomy
requirement.requirement: Worker taxonomy supported by the framework: file scanning (pre-commit / pre-push), prompt-injection check (UserPromptSubmit — returns additionalContext), post-response audit (Stop), log publishing (UserPromptSubmit + Stop -> Kafka), boot orchestration (SessionStart), and mode selection (SessionStart). Each is a concrete subclass of EnforcementWorker, deployed as its own standalone executable.

story.name: Scanning: file enumeration on hooks, SCOPES evaluation, scope precedence
story.description: Per V20 §4.5 and §4.9. Workers receive resource candidates (staged or about-to-push files for the V1 ScanFilesEnforcementWorker), evaluate each via the base-class is_in_scope walk against the SCOPES rows on the enforcement entry, and dispatch matched check methods. Scope precedence is fixed and lives entirely in the base class.

requirement.name: Scope walk precedence
requirement.requirement: Scope evaluation is fixed-precedence and lives entirely in the base class. For each (resource, function_name) the base class walks the matching rows in self.scopes (filtered by function_name) in this fixed order: excluded_exact, excluded_pattern, allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, then per-check SCOPE_DEFAULT. Subclasses do not override this walk. The default behavior (in scope vs. out of scope when no row matched) is declared per check via the per-method SCOPE_DEFAULT class attribute.

requirement.name: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker
requirement.requirement: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker (worked example, V1) lives at projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/scan_files_enforcement_worker.py. It is a standalone Python script with a main that takes enforcement_id as a CLI argument and exits with a status code. Its run implements two domain checks synchronously, in this order, on every in-scope file: (a) _scan_http(file) — the HTTP-vs-HTTPS regex scan ported from preCommitScan.py; (b) _validate_json(file) — the JSON schema validation ported from validate_all_json.py. Both run inside the same subprocess. Multi-threading inside run is a documented future enhancement, not V1. requires_lock = false (read-only worker; the manager dispatches without acquiring a lock). ScanFilesEnforcementWorker's scope-list rules live in its enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json under the scopes field (see §4.6); the worker inherits the default _load_scopes from EnforcementWorker, which returns self.entry.get("scopes", []). It does NOT override _load_scopes and contributes no SCOPES class attribute (see §4.5 for the mechanism, §4.9.1 for the per-method spec, and §4.9.2 for the worked-example rows).

requirement.name: Scope rows on enforcement entry
requirement.requirement: ScanFilesEnforcementWorker scope rules are expressed as a flat three-column list in its enforcement entry in engineering_rules.json under the scopes field. Each row has the shape [function_name: str, scope_list_type: str, list_of_terms: list[str]] where scope_list_type is one of the four canonical terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern) and function_name is the name of a check method on the worker (e.g. _scan_http, _validate_json). The EnforcementWorker base class loads the list at worker startup through the virtual _load_scopes method, whose default implementation returns self.entry.get("scopes", []); ScanFilesEnforcementWorker inherits that default and does NOT override it. The base class then resolves function_name to a bound method via getattr(self, row[0]) at startup, so a typo in function_name fails loudly rather than silently dropping a rule. The ordered precedence of the four types is fixed in the base class per TR-5 and is described in narrative form in §4.5. The SCOPE_DEFAULT class attribute is per-check: False for _scan_http (don't flag a path that no rule matched), True for _validate_json (every governed JSON is in scope unless explicitly excluded). The canonical worked example — exactly the rows used by V1 — is in §4.9.2.

requirement.name: preCommitScan.py JSON retirement
requirement.requirement: preCommitScan.py SHALL drop ".json" from SCAN_EXTENSIONS and \.json$ from HTTP_EXEMPT_PATTERNS once ScanFilesEnforcementWorker is the single source of truth (note: SCAN_EXTENSIONS and HTTP_EXEMPT_PATTERNS are legacy module-level names inside preCommitScan.py — the artifact being retired — and are not part of the new framework's vocabulary; the new framework uses scopes rows in engineering_rules.json). Once the manager dispatches all enforcement, preCommitScan.py is retired.

requirement.name: Scan must test this content
requirement.requirement: The scan rule Must test for: (a) Font compliance — see EPIC-008-F-011-S-003-REQ-B-004 (Scan of all relevant files must test font compliance); (b) JSON Schema validation — see EPIC-008-F-002-S-006 (JSON validation: _validate_json check, $schema web-fetch resolver, meta-schema carve-out, in-run cache); (c) HTTPS compliance — see EPIC-008-F-002-S-005 (HTTP vs HTTPS: _scan_http check and allowed_pattern URL handling).

story.name: HTTP vs HTTPS: _scan_http check and allowed_pattern URL handling
story.description: Per V20 BR-12, BR-13, TR-11. The _scan_http check on ScanFilesEnforcementWorker enforces that production source code, documentation, and deployment configuration MUST NOT contain http:// URLs unless the URL itself matches an allowed_pattern row on the enforcement entry's scopes (loopback, link-local metadata, w3.org, etc.). Files intended to carry http:// content as legitimate data are listed in allowed_exact / allowed_pattern rows. Other files are exempted via excluded_exact / excluded_pattern.

requirement.name: http: legitimate-content allowance
requirement.requirement: Files that are intended to carry plain text "http:" as legitimate content — for example, JSON files whose purpose is to record example URLs, configuration files that list http endpoints by design, fixtures, and similar data files — MUST be allowed to contain the term "http:". These files are listed on the enforcement entry's allowed by exact match rows, or matched by the enforcement entry's allowed by pattern rows, and they will not be flagged as a violation.

requirement.name: http: production-source ban
requirement.requirement: Files that are intended to be production source code, documentation, deployment configuration, or any other artifact that should not embed insecure http URLs MUST NOT contain the term "http:" unless the URL itself is on the enforcement entry's allowed by pattern rows (for example, loopback addresses, link-local metadata endpoints, or known public standards URLs). Files of this kind that are deliberately exempt for any reason MUST appear on the enforcement entry's excluded by exact match rows or be matched by the enforcement entry's excluded by pattern rows. Any other file found to contain the term "http:" is a violation and the commit MUST be blocked.

requirement.name: _scan_http scope alignment
requirement.requirement: The set of files allowed to contain "http:" is exactly the union of the enforcement entry's allowed_exact rows and the files matched by the entry's allowed_pattern rows for _scan_http. The set of files exempt from the scan entirely is exactly the union of the entry's excluded_exact rows and the files matched by the entry's excluded_pattern rows for _scan_http. Any file not matched by any of those four scope_list_type rows that contains the term "http:" — except where the URL itself matches an allowed_pattern row for _scan_http — is a violation.

story.name: JSON validation: _validate_json check, $schema web-fetch resolver, meta-schema carve-out, in-run cache
story.description: Per V20 BR-11/15/16, TR-12/18/19, §4.9.3 and §4.9.3.1. The _validate_json check on ScanFilesEnforcementWorker validates every governed JSON file under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ against the schema declared in its $schema field, using jsonschema Draft 2020-12. ChatHealthy schemas declared in $schema URLs are resolved via HTTPS GET (5s timeout, per-run cache) per TR-18; the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema is the single carve-out, served from a local copy under Website/schemas/standard/ per TR-19 / BR-16. Files with $schema missing that are not explicitly excluded MUST FAIL LOUD.

requirement.name: Governed JSON validation gate
requirement.requirement: Every file the system treats as governed JSON content MUST validate cleanly against the schema declared in its $schema field. The set of governed JSON files is defined using only the four permitted scope-list terms (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern). The system MUST NOT trust data from a JSON file that fails schema validation, and the framework MUST treat validation failure as a governance violation. JSON validation is the load-bearing gate that protects the entire governed-data layer from silent drift.

requirement.name: Draft 2020-12, no opt-out
requirement.requirement: Governed JSON content lives under brain/machine_artifacts/content/. Each governed JSON file MUST declare its schema URL in a top-level $schema field. JSON parsing uses Python's standard library json module. Schema validation uses the jsonschema package against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Validation failure produces a violation record per TR-6 and contributes to the worker's exit code (EXIT_VIOLATIONS_FOUND = 1). Files identified by the worker's excluded_exact or excluded_pattern lists are skipped silently; files in scope without a $schema field MUST FAIL LOUD. There is no opt-out, and there is no quiet passing of unschemaed JSON content. The JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema URL is the single resolver carve-out, served from a local copy at Website/schemas/standard/json-schema-2020-12-meta.json. All other $schema URLs are resolved by HTTP GET with a 5-second timeout and per-run cache.

requirement.name: Validation uses $schema URL
requirement.requirement: Validation MUST use the schema referenced by the JSON file's $schema URL.

requirement.name: External standards committed
requirement.requirement: External standards used by the framework MUST be committed to the repository.

requirement.name: $schema HTTPS resolution + cache
requirement.requirement: Aligned to BR-15. ChatHealthy schemas declared in $schema URLs are resolved via HTTPS GET to the URL the JSON file declared, performed at validation time. A per-run cache deduplicates identical URLs within a single worker invocation. Unreachable URL, non-200, timeout, or non-JSON response body produces a per-file ViolationRecord per TR-6.

requirement.name: External-standard carve-out cache
requirement.requirement: Aligned to BR-16. Cached external standards live under Website/schemas/standard/. A standard is eligible for caching when its URL is contractually frozen by the spec maintainer (any change requires a new versioned URL). The framework's runtime serves those URLs from the cached copies. Cached standards remain under the stewardship of their original publisher; the framework's governance applies to content the framework owns.

story.name: SessionStart and PostCompact boot duties dispatched via chathealthy_enforcement_manager
story.description: On every Claude Code SessionStart hook and on every PostCompact hook (context purge), the boot program replays the most recent conversation utterances from MongoDB and injects the agile_backlog taxonomy. Dispatch is performed by chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py per Rule-002 enforcement entries; the boot is no longer wired directly in .claude/settings.json.

requirement.name: Replay 170 most recent utterances from Mongo into SessionStart additionalContext
requirement.requirement: On SessionStart, chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST read the 170 most recent utterance documents from MongoDB ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive, trim each document to {actor, content}, order newest-first, and emit them as part of the hook's additionalContext so Claude resumes with recent conversation context. If the MongoDB read fails (connection, auth, or query error), the boot MUST fail open - log the failure to stderr and continue with remaining SessionStart duties without aborting the session.

requirement.name: Inject agile_backlog taxonomy (epic+feature descriptions, story names) into SessionStart additionalContext
requirement.requirement: On SessionStart, chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST read brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json and emit the business taxonomy as part of the hook's additionalContext: every epic's id, name, and description; every feature's id, name, and description; every story's id and name. Story descriptions, requirements, and tests MUST NOT be emitted. The output is the operator-facing context shape, not a context-resident @-import.

requirement.requirement: Each Claude Code session MUST complete a deterministic, non-circumventable boot sequence before any other work. The sequence is: (1) load the governance brain and run compliance checks; (2) at the end of boot, ask the user exactly two questions in order and block all other assistant output until both are answered — Q1: mode selection per REQ-010; Q2: orphan triage per REQ-011. The sequence MUST NOT be skippable, paraphrasable, summarizable, or deferrable by Claude Code. Implementation MAY use any hook topology (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop-hook validator, blocking-reply pattern) so long as the user-observable behavior holds: every new session begins with those two questions presented verbatim, in order, with no other assistant output preceding them.

requirement.requirement: Orphan triage is the second of the two boot questions. After the user answers REQ-010, Claude Code MUST ask a single yes/no question: 'Triage orphan bugs?' If the user answers no, boot completes and normal work begins. If the user answers yes, Claude Code MUST present the orphan bug table and the user chooses how many to triage this boot — one, several, or all. Triaging an orphan means assigning it a req_id or closing it. There is no per-orphan defer option and no obligation to triage every orphan; the single yes/no gate governs whether the list is shown at all, and within 'yes' the user drives how many get worked.
requirement.name: Boot question: Ask user 'Triage orphan bugs?' and present table if answered yes

requirement.requirement: Three context-resident artifacts MUST be loaded into the Claude Code session context at every session start, and MUST be re-injected after any context compaction: (1) brain/machine_artifacts/content/bugs.json — active bug register, loaded in full; (2) brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json — engineering rules, loaded in full; (3) _oneshots/test_output/backlog_stories.json — story-level pruned view of agile_backlog.json covering Epic → Feature → Story only. The story view carries story metadata (story_id, title, description, parent_feature, sprint, size, status, accepted_by, orphan, approval) plus an integer requirement_count per story. It does NOT carry requirement bodies, pytest pointers, realized_by arrays, or any node below story. The full agile_backlog.json (~521K tokens) is NOT context-resident; specific requirement bodies, pytest ids, and realized_by data MUST be fetched from the canonical brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json via Read when Claude needs them. Canonical brain content lives on disk under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ and is never stored anywhere else. The story view is a derived artifact — gitignored, regenerated at session start from the canonical source — it does not replace the source. A pytest MUST verify: (a) @-imports for the three context-resident artifacts are present in the root CLAUDE.md; (b) every current file under Code/DataPipelines/ matching the listed extensions (minus excluded dirs) has a corresponding @-import; (c) every @-imported file exists and is non-empty; (d) no @-imported path is stale. A git pre-commit hook MUST regenerate the DataPipelines @-import block when any file under Code/DataPipelines/ is added, moved, or deleted; if the block is stale, pre-commit MUST fail. Purpose: these artifacts are the ones Claude is most prone to shortcut-reasoning about — grepping instead of reading, guessing instead of checking, proposing duplicates because the original was never loaded. Making the backlog's high-level shape (9 epics / 83 features / 301 stories) context-resident removes the option to grep-and-punt for structure. Requirement bodies remain on-demand because loading the full backlog at ~521K tokens would consume more than half the 1M context window for content that is rarely needed in full. History: agile_backlog.json was attempted in context-residency 2026-04-18 and was replaced with the story-level view the same day. EPIC-008-F-003-S-002-REQ-T-003 (the flat pipe-delimited req_index.txt view) is deprecated in favor of this story-tree view. API source: Claude Code memory docs at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md — '@path/to/import' syntax, 'Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch', 'CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length', 'Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session.' Hook-based injection is NOT a viable substitute because per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks cap additionalContext at 10,000 characters with overflow saved to file + preview — too small for these artifacts.

requirement.requirement: Per-artifact load confirmation. After each session boot, the diagnostic MUST emit one confirmation line per context-resident artifact as defined in REQ-012. Each line MUST cite the full project-relative path of the artifact. Silent success is not permitted. The diagnostic signal may come from the InstructionsLoaded hook log, a direct content canary, or both; the reporting format is one line per artifact regardless of source. This requirement MUST NOT name specific artifacts — REQ-012 is the single source of truth for the artifact list; any change to scope belongs there, not here.
requirement.name: Emit one confirmation line per context-resident artifact after session boot

requirement.requirement: Load-failure short message. If any context-resident brain artifact fails load verification at session boot (per REQ-012 and REQ-017), the diagnostic MUST output a single short failure line (one line, under 200 characters) that names the failing artifact and classifies the failure as exactly one of four reasons — no more, no less: invalid_json | hash_unreadable | not_loaded | hash_mismatch. A long explanation is a violation of this requirement — follow-up detail belongs in a separate report, not the verdict line.
requirement.name: Short one-line artifact load failure message with exact reason classification

requirement.requirement: Load verification procedure. For each context-resident artifact as defined in REQ-012, the diagnostic MUST execute exactly four steps in order, short-circuiting on the first failure: (1) validate the file as JSON — on failure emit 'invalid_json'; (2) compute sha256 of the file on disk and retain it — on I/O or hash failure emit 'hash_unreadable'; (3) confirm the harness loaded the file into context (InstructionsLoaded event fired for that file_path) — on absence emit 'not_loaded'; (4) recompute sha256 at the InstructionsLoaded event and compare to the hash from step 2 — on inequality emit 'hash_mismatch'. If all four steps pass, emit one 'LOADED' line per REQ-015. These four failure reasons are exhaustive: the diagnostic MUST NOT introduce a fifth category (e.g. timeout, truncation, attention_drift, unknown). Any observed failure that does not map to one of the four reasons is a gap in the procedure, not a new reason. This requirement MUST NOT name specific artifacts — REQ-012 is the single source of truth for the artifact list.
requirement.name: Verify context-resident artifacts using four-step diagnostic with strict error,

requirement.requirement: Before creating any bug record in brain/machine_artifacts/content/bugs.json, Claude MUST search the register for a semantically duplicate or closely-related existing bug and update the existing record rather than create a new one when a match is found. When no logical parent requirement exists: in Normal or Idiot Mode (v4-004) Claude MUST escalate to human and wait for a decision before inserting; in Unattended Mode Claude MUST insert the bug with req_id = ORPHAN_BUG, flag it for human's async review at the next boot's orphan triage, and proceed with its work.
requirement.name: Prevent bug duplication; update existing or escalate/flag if no parent exists

requirement.requirement: Before creating any requirement, story, feature, or epic in brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json, Claude MUST search the backlog for a semantically duplicate or closely-related existing entry and update the existing record rather than create a new one when a match is found. Updates MUST focus on conciseness, accuracy, and fidelity to the evidence. When the entry is novel, Claude MUST insert it under a logical parent — requirement under story, story under feature, feature under epic. When no logical parent exists: in Normal or Idiot Mode (v4-004) Claude MUST escalate to human and wait for a decision before inserting; in Unattended Mode Claude MUST insert the entry with orphan = true under the nearest ancestor, flag it for human's async review, and proceed with its work.
requirement.name: Search backlog for duplicates before inserting new agile artifacts

feature.name: Audit — Technical, Business, Regulatory and Corporate Governance
feature.description: This feature encompasses all the audits that must be done to maintain technical and business history, integrity and regulatory and corporate governance.

story.description: A deterministic Python orchestrator dispatches disposable AI workers to analyze git history, brain artifacts, and current code to identify lost capabilities, undocumented changes, and gaps between intent and implementation. The orchestrator is 100% deterministic — all state is on disk, all decisions are file-existence checks. AI is used only inside workers for code analysis. Audits MUST NOT create state changes — they only maintain their own notes and documents, and produce findings and recommendations. The orchestrator loops until all jobs are complete or a human sets the stop command in the control file.

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST examine every version of every file in the git repository to establish a complete lineage of what was built, changed, and removed.
requirement.name: Audit all file versions for complete git repository lineage

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every capability that the brain documents as intended but that does not exist in the current codebase. The brain is the authoritative source of intent.
requirement.name: Identify capabilities intended by brain but missing from current codebase

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every capability that was built and subsequently lost due to uncontrolled changes, code rollbacks, or data loss.
requirement.name: Audit identifies capabilities lost via uncontrolled change, rollback, or data

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every AI call, system prompt, and LLM integration that existed in any previous version and determine whether it is active, intentionally replaced, or lost.
requirement.name: Audit all past AI calls, prompts, LLMs; flag active, replaced, or lost ones

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST cross-reference all findings against the agile backlog, bugs, design documents, business plan, work log, punch lists, unrealized ideas, and all other brain artifacts to determine whether each loss is documented or undocumented.
requirement.name: Audit cross-checks findings against all artifacts for documented or undocumented

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST produce findings categorized as: undocumented losses, documented but unplanned recoveries, and intentional replacements. Each finding MUST include evidence from git history or brain artifacts.
requirement.name: Categorize audit findings; each must include git or brain evidence

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST produce actionable recommendations for each finding, prioritized by user impact, with effort estimates and a proposed recovery approach.
requirement.name: Audit recommendations prioritized by user impact with effort and recovery plan

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST be repeatable. Running the audit again on the same codebase MUST produce the same findings. The audit is idempotent.
requirement.name: Audit must be repeatable and idempotent, yielding same findings on same codebase

requirement.requirement: The audit output MUST be consumable by both humans (readable report) and machines (structured JSON). The CEO is the primary consumer.
requirement.name: Audit output as human-readable report and structured JSON for CEO consumption

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST NOT modify any source code, database records, brain files, or deployed artifacts. It is a read-only operation. Output is limited to the audit directory only.
requirement.name: Audit is read-only, modifies nothing, output limited to audit directory

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST run to completion autonomously without requiring human intervention beyond the initial start command.
requirement.name: Audit runs autonomously to completion after initial start command

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST survive infrastructure failures (crashes, restarts, context loss) and resume from the last completed unit of work.
requirement.name: Audit recovers from failures and resumes from last completed unit of work

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST track and report its own cost (token consumption) as part of its output.
requirement.name: Audit must track and report its own token consumption in its output

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST have numbered findings where the most important findings are at the top with the lowest number and the least important findings have the highest numbers.
requirement.name: Audit findings numbered by importance, highest priority at top

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST make recommendations based on the findings of how to address and remediate each finding.
requirement.name: Audit must recommend remediations for each finding

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST describe its methodology at the top of the report.
requirement.name: Audit report must include methodology description at the top

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST document its assumptions under methodology and above findings.
requirement.name: Audit documents assumptions under methodology and above findings

requirement.requirement: Each audit finding MUST be supported with evidence of at least one example from both the codebase (which may be that no code exists) and from the brain (a known best practice, a brain artifact reference, or code with file and line ranges).
requirement.name: Audit finding must cite code and brain evidence examples

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST be a pure Python script with no AI dependencies. All decisions MUST be based on file existence checks and JSON parsing. No LLM calls in the orchestrator.
requirement.name: Pure Python orchestrator with file checks, JSON parsing, no AI or LLM calls

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST loop continuously until all jobs are complete or a human sets the command to stop in the control file. No other mechanism may stop the orchestrator.
requirement.name: Orchestrator loops until all jobs finish or control file stop command is set

requirement.requirement: All orchestrator state MUST be persisted to disk in a control file (control.json). The orchestrator MUST NOT depend on Claude Code context or conversation memory for any decision.
requirement.name: Persist orchestrator state to control.json; no reliance on memory for decisions

requirement.requirement: Each job MUST write a checkpoint file to disk upon completion. If the orchestrator restarts after a crash, it MUST skip completed jobs by checking for existing checkpoint files.
requirement.name: Write checkpoint files on job completion; skip completed jobs after restart

requirement.requirement: AI workers MUST be spawned as disposable agents with no prior context. Each worker receives a self-contained prompt from a file and writes its output to a checkpoint file. Workers have no knowledge of the orchestrator or other workers.
requirement.name: Spawn disposable AI workers with isolated, self-contained prompts and outputs

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST record token usage and duration from each worker in the control file. Total token spend MUST be visible to the human at all times via the control file.
requirement.name: Record per-worker token usage/duration; show total spend in control file

requirement.requirement: All worker output MUST use structured JSON with predefined schemas. No free-form text output. Every finding MUST include evidence (commit hash, file path, or brain file reference).
requirement.name: Worker output uses structured JSON schemas with evidence for every finding

requirement.requirement: The audit output MUST be expressed as a JSON document having a strict schema. The output MUST be in strict compliance with that schema.
requirement.name: Audit output as JSON document with strict schema compliance

story.name: Codebase History Audit — Deterministic Agent

story.description: Two-pass scanner: Pass 1 streams every source file, builds a map of all definitions (classes, methods, functions) and all references (calls, imports, attribute access). Pass 2 reconciles — anything defined but never referenced is dead and must be deleted. Two modes: check-in (staged files only, fast) and full regression (entire codebase).

requirement.requirement: Pass 1 must stream source files without holding full source in memory. It accumulates a definitions map (name, file, line) and a references set (names used). Memory proportional to symbol count, not source size. DR-008 compliant.
requirement.name: Stream pass 1 source, accumulate symbol maps, memory ~symbol count, DR-008

requirement.requirement: Pass 2 walks the definitions map and checks each against the references set. Any definition with zero references and no framework-invocation decorator (FastAPI route, Azure trigger, governance hook) is reported as dead code.
requirement.name: Report unreferenced definitions without framework decorators as dead code in Pas

requirement.requirement: Check-in mode scans only staged files (git diff --cached). If a staged file adds a function, verify something calls it. If it deletes a function, verify nothing else calls it. Must complete in under 5 seconds for typical commits.
requirement.name: Check-in scans staged files for function usage and finishes under 5 seconds

requirement.requirement: Dead code found during check-in mode blocks the commit. Dead code found during full regression is reported but does not block (informational for promotion review).
requirement.name: Block commits for dead code in check-in; report only in full regression

story.name: Run Time Error Management
story.description: Defines and enforces runtime error behavior for the ChatHealthy.AI front-end application. This story covers how the application surfaces failures to users, how it interacts with backend services under failure conditions.

requirement.name: Fatal error full-screen display in index.html
requirement.requirement: For every error that is fatal — meaning any error condition whatsoever that is not explicitly required in a written requirement to be less than fatal — index.html is to display the following: In a large font and centered: 'HTTP 503: Fatal Error, this service is not available.' In a smaller font and centered: Line 1: link to HTTPS://{current environment}.chathealthy.ai. Line 2: If you get this error repeatedly and wish to call our team, please call Skip Snow @ 646 408 8999. Line 3: If you prefer email skip's email is: skip@chatHealthy.ai. Line 4: smaller text that wraps, the error message returned from an API. If the error is from the JavaScript without a call to an API then the error message will be 'JS routine {failed}'. Line 5: we apologize for this problem.

requirement.name: Internal API error responses must not reveal application facts
requirement.requirement: Every API that index.html calls that is internal to ChatHealthy.ai's servers must, when they encounter errors, return an error message that is not sufficiently clear that it would reveal any significant fact about the application. The error message can cite the API that failed, the rough-grained source of the error, and the time of the error.

requirement.name: API errors must log a detailed message for later debugging
requirement.requirement: Any API that does encounter an error must log a detailed message about the error so that it can be debugged later.

story.name: Use of HTTP methods for ChatHealthy.ai

requirement.name: Client-callable endpoints exposed exclusively over POST and OPTIONS; other methods rejected
requirement.requirement: Every endpoint on a ChatHealthy.ai's dynamic web servers (currently hosted by HuggingFace) MUST only accept the HTTPS POST and OPTIONS Methods. These server MUST reject any other HTTPS method on those endpoints by returning HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed.

requirement.name: All ChatHealthy.ai web servers redirect HTTP to HTTPS

The local development enviornmnet's web server SHALL also support the GET and HEAD methods. OPTIONS Will explictly not be suported by Cloudflare. These servers will return 405s.
