story.name: Uniformly Control ChatHealthyFonts
story.description: It is required that font sizes not be hard coded anywhere in ChatHealthy's application portfolio. This story specifies the requirements that allow for granular control of fonts via API throughout the application.

requirement.name: Font formatting of display text confined to web-tier files: HTML, CSS, JS, SVG, or TS Pages Functions
requirement.requirement: No formatting of display information of text fonts CAN be hosted anywhere but on the web server in static HTML, JavaScript, CSS, SVG, or TypeScript (Cloudflare Pages Functions) files.

requirement.name: Common function must format fonts
requirement.requirement: One common front end function used by every declaration of any font function must be supported. This function must have a set of default arguments so it can be called without any arguments. The arguments must allow for all variance in fonts allowed by HTML, and must as necessary be cognizant of the target environment, e.g. html, css, js etc.

requirement.name: Default font to be defined
requirement.requirement: A base default font must be defined, and changeable from one and only one file. The function defined in B-002 Must use these defaults. The default Must be contained in the same file as the function that is called by all of the instances of fonts in the application.

requirement.name: Scan of all relevant files must test font compliance

This scan will be implemented as part of Rule-008 (All files added to the local Git repository must be scanned for architectural compliance), not as a new engineering rule.

story.name: AI embedding Model must be Uniform across the entire application
story.description: Establishes the single canonical embedding model used across ChatHealthy.AI. Any embedding-generation use-site requirement MUST reference the canonical requirement here rather than restate the model name. (see EPIC-008-F-011-S-004-REQ-B-001)

requirement.name: Single canonical embedding model for ChatHealthy.AI
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy.AI's only embedding model is OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (vector dimension 3072). Every requirement that mandates embedding generation MUST reference this requirement (EPIC-008-F-011-S-004-REQ-B-001) rather than restate the model name. Code that generates embeddings MUST use this model.

story.name: Uniform application logging
story.description: App-wide rules for runtime logging — uniform logging surface, framework choice, environment-driven configuration. Tool subclasses inherit logging from the base class; no per-tool ad-hoc logging or third-party logger calls.

requirement.name: ChatHealthyTool base class implements uniform tool-invocation logging via Python's stdlib logging
requirement.requirement: The ChatHealthyTool base class MUST be the sole logging surface for every tool invocation. Every concrete subclass is logged uniformly by the base class — no concrete tool implements its own logging path, and no concrete tool emits print(), ad-hoc file writes, or third-party logger calls inside the dispatch chain. The base class MUST use Python's standard library logging module; logger configuration MUST be via logging.config.dictConfig so handlers, formatters, and per-environment behavior are declarative. Log messages MUST be suppressible by level via environment variable — the operator sets LOG_LEVEL (DEBUG / INFO / WARNING / ERROR / CRITICAL) in the runtime environment, and the logger MUST respect that threshold and drop lower-priority messages. The logger MUST support writing to both stdout and stderr (configurable per level — e.g., errors to stderr, normal logs to stdout). Third-party logging libraries (loguru, structlog) are forbidden in the tool dispatch path. Each log entry MUST include tool_name, redacted input args, output result, duration in ms, and any exception with traceback.

feature.name: Deployment
feature.description: The deployment feature is where ChatHealthy translates its business taxonomy (agile_backlog.json) into its digital taxonomy (architecture.json). Two models, one map. Every deployment-centric artifact lives here, nowhere else; deployment requirements from other features point at requirements inside this feature.

story.name: Universal deploy contract
story.description: The 'deployment_architecture.json' currently hosted by 'the brain and residing in firm's cursor project's 'file system' as well as in GITHUB is the single source of truth for all deployment facts for ChatHealthy.ai's components. This file must be the source of One local and one remote deploys script. It must, regardless of environment, contain all necessary information to do full deployments to each required component. This includes fulsome facts about code branches, or the local file directories for the local build. These facts include but are not limited to port assignments, atomicity, source code file facts, secrets and environment keys must be included, but the secrets may never be in any file that is part of a build package. Each deployment must have an enforced human-authorization gate. A build script for each remote component must build a release package stored in GIT Hub with appropriate Version information. And All builds must be done on a local workstation, and then shipped via a deploy script, which will also be accountable to build and configure the components as necessary.

requirement.name: Port table
requirement.requirement: Canonical port assignments, identical across all environments (local, dev, qa, prod): port 80 (HTTP — 301 redirects to HTTPS), port 443 (Website wrapper — public HTTPS entry), port 7860 (FindCare backend), port 8001 (EvaluateCare backend), port 8002 (SharedServices backend + React frontend). Every other requirement that names a port MUST refer to this requirement; MUST NOT restate the table.

requirement.name: Atomic deploy
requirement.requirement: Each deploy script either succeeds totally or fails totally with the environment torn down. There is no half-deployed third state. Atomicity is enforced by tearing down the previous environment as the first step (precondition; the ports in REQ-T-001 cannot host two services simultaneously).

requirement.name: Target readiness check
requirement.requirement: Before any deploy action, the script verifies the target environment is reachable and able to receive a deployment. For local: every port in REQ-T-001 is reachable on the host. For deployed envs: the target HuggingFace Space exists and accepts GitHub Actions pushes.

requirement.name: Build, start, verify
requirement.requirement: The script builds all components, starts them, then waits until every component responds as expected. The components are: FindCare backend, EvaluateCare backend, SharedServices backend (serving the React frontend), the public HTTPS entry (Website wrapper for local; Cloudflare Pages for deployed envs), and the front-end MongoDB cluster (tested as available, never deployed).

requirement.name: Smoke test invocation
requirement.requirement: After build/start/verify, the script invokes the master smoke test (S-006) with the target environment as parameter. On smoke-test failure the script MUST request explicit human verification before tearing down the environment, so the operator can inspect the failed state. Atomic teardown (REQ-B-001) proceeds only after the human authorizes it. Verification type = UAT (the human-verify gate on smoke failure cannot be auto-tested without stubbing the human, which defeats the requirement); UAT step lives in Code/deploy/local_deploy.py.

requirement.name: Step notices
requirement.requirement: Between every significant deploy step the script emits a notice via the mechanism defined in S-007. No bell rings unless explicitly instructed by the operator per S-007.

requirement.name: Human authorization gate
requirement.requirement: Every deploy — local, dev, qa, prod — pauses and requires explicit human authorization (interactive confirmation or signed approval token) before the production-affecting action begins. There are no unattended deploys now or in the foreseeable future. Production deploys carry the same gate as any other; what differs in prod is the version/framework ID assignment that follows (see S-004).

requirement.name: No commit or deploy without explicit human authorization
requirement.requirement: No commit or deploy CAN take place without explicit human authorization. A commit represents a human-vetted release candidate; the push that immediately follows is implicit in the commit's authorization and does not require a separate authorization event. This requirement shall be enforced as part of ChatHealthy's rule enforcement prior to an Anthropic hook for code-control integration.

requirement.name: Version document
requirement.requirement: Build, version, and framework identifiers live as a single MongoDB document on the front-end cluster `chathealthyfrontend`, in the global database `admin`, in the collection literally named `Versions`. Each change inserts a new record carrying all three fields (build, version, framework) plus a `from` timestamp; the latest record by `from` is the current state. All three backend /health endpoints read the latest record. Build is incremented by the build-bump rule (REQ-T-003). Version and framework are set only by humans during prod deploy (S-004). Deploy pipelines never write these fields directly; the rule and the human routine are the only writers.

requirement.name: Build-bump rule
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule (Rule-063 in `engineering_rules.json`) executes as a post-commit hook on every commit not part of a deploy pipeline. Statement 1: insert a new `admin.Versions` record with build incremented by exactly one; version and framework copied forward unchanged. Statement 2: push the new values to the running Kafka producer's `/version_bump` endpoint so subsequent messages carry the new build stamp without the producer re-reading MongoDB.

requirement.name: Atomic teardown precondition
requirement.requirement: Before build, the script wipes prior artifacts and running processes (including Docker containers) and verifies every port in REQ-T-001 is clear. The wipe is the precondition that enables atomicity (REQ-B-001).

requirement.name: Structured deploy output
requirement.requirement: The script writes a structured output file Claude can read to {projectRoot}/_oneshots/test_output/deploy/ with the environment name and timestamp in the filename. Contents: pass/fail per test, container IDs (or PIDs for the Website wrapper), port assignments (per REQ-T-001), timestamps, and errors.

requirement.name: Pytest exit propagation
requirement.requirement: When piping pytest output through tee, the script uses PIPESTATUS[0] (not $?) to capture the pytest exit code. On any pytest step failure, SMOKE TEST FAILED MUST be displayed to the human operator on the controlling terminal (not silently logged) so the operator can act before any teardown decision per REQ-B-004.

requirement.name: React frontend build
requirement.requirement: Each deploy script builds the React frontend with the backend API URL for the target environment baked in, pointing to the service serving the React frontend per S-001-REQ-T-001 (post-S-008 migration: SharedServices on port 8002). Local and deployed envs differ only in the domain portion of the URL.

requirement.name: Deployment definition is the persisted collection of TargetRecords
requirement.requirement: The deployment definition MUST be the persisted collection of TargetRecord documents. Each persisted document IS one TargetRecord (one deployment target's full definition across every environment in which that target is realized); the COLLECTION of all such documents IS the deployment definition as a whole. No single document IS the deployment definition. No document MAY carry more than one target_id. No document MAY carry a child collection that aggregates multiple targets. The writer MUST persist exactly one document per target_id and the loader MUST treat the collection (not any individual document) as the authoritative deployment definition.

requirement.name: TargetRecord top-level shape is the closed four-key target-keyed object
requirement.requirement: Every TargetRecord MUST be a single object whose top-level required keys are exactly, and only, `target_id`, `target_kind`, `environments`, and `files`. The top-level object MUST be closed (`additionalProperties: false`). No other top-level key MAY appear in any TargetRecord. The schema's `$id` MUST be `https://dev.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyDeploymentArchitectureSchema.json` and the schema document MUST be JSON Schema Draft 2020-12.

requirement.name: TargetRecord carries no `metadata` field anywhere
requirement.requirement: The field name `metadata` MUST NOT appear at any object level in any TargetRecord. The top-level TargetRecord, every entry in `environments[]`, every entry in `files[]`, and every nested object reachable from any of those MUST NOT contain a key named `metadata`. The schema MUST forbid the key by virtue of `additionalProperties: false` at every object level combined with the required-keys lists. The writer MUST reject any candidate record carrying a `metadata` key at any level before persisting.

requirement.name: target_id is opaque and unique within the deployment collection
requirement.requirement: Every `target_id` MUST be opaque (e.g. `target_001`) and MUST NOT encode any business product, service, or feature name; its syntactic shape MUST match the regex declared in the schema (`^target_[a-z0-9_]{1,64}$`). Within the persisted deployment collection, the set of `target_id` values MUST be unique. DeploymentCollection MUST raise on any attempted insert whose `target_id` already exists in the collection; the uniqueness violation is a hard-fail with no auto-rename, no warning, and no soft path. The collection size is data-driven; no consumer of the schema MAY hard-code a target count.

requirement.name: target_kind taxonomy is closed with no catchall
requirement.requirement: Every `target_kind` value MUST be a member of the closed enum declared in the V18 schema: `hf_space` | `cloudflare_pages_project` | `azure_function_app` | `host_os_process` | `docker_local_container` | `mongodb_collection` | `github_actions_workflow_runner`. The taxonomy is CLOSED. No catchall value (including but not limited to `"other"`) MAY exist in the enum. A value outside the enum MUST cause schema validation to hard-fail. Adding a new class of deployment target MUST be done by revising the schema; there is no escape hatch in the data.

requirement.name: environments[] is the target's per-environment binding inventory
requirement.requirement: Every TargetRecord MUST carry an `environments[]` array of at least one entry (`minItems: 1`, `uniqueItems: true`). Each entry MUST be a closed object with exactly the required fields `env_binding` and `node_address`. `env_binding` MUST be a member of the closed enum; `node_address` MUST be a non-empty string within the length bound declared in the schema (`minLength: 1`, `maxLength: 1024`). The inventory is data-driven; the schema MUST NOT hard-code a count of environments per target.

requirement.name: env_binding values are unique within a single TargetRecord's environments[]
requirement.requirement: Within a single TargetRecord, the set of `env_binding` values across `environments[]` MUST be unique: a target maps to at most one `node_address` per environment. The schema declares this invariant in the description of the `environments` property; the writer and the crosswalk validator MUST enforce it at gate time and MUST reject any record carrying two `environments[]` entries with the same `env_binding`. The reject is a hard-fail; there is no soft path.

requirement.name: env_binding taxonomy is closed and sourced from the project env vocabulary
requirement.requirement: Every `env_binding` value MUST be a member of the closed enum declared in the schema: `local` | `dev` | `qa` | `prod`. The enum's values MUST be a subset of the project's existing env-vocabulary source-of-truth cited in the schema description: `VALID_ENVS` in `Code/Shared/ops/bump_build.py` and `Code/Shared/ops/set_version_framework.py`; `ENV_ORDER` in `Code/Shared/ops/promote_build.py` and `Code/Shared/ops/migrate_versions_to_per_env.py`; deploy-test choices in `Code/deploy/conftest.py`. Any value outside the enum MUST cause schema validation to hard-fail.

requirement.name: node_address is a templated string; substitution belongs to software
requirement.requirement: Every `environments[i].node_address` MUST be a non-empty string within the length bound declared in the schema. Template tokens MAY appear in the value; the schema MUST NOT declare any substitution rule, enumerate any token, or constrain the address form (URL, host:port, connection string, registry path, etc.). Resolution-time substitution semantics MUST live in software, not in this schema.

requirement.name: files[] is the target's source-file composition inventory; every field required
requirement.requirement: Every TargetRecord MUST carry a `files[]` array. Each entry MUST be a closed object with exactly the required fields `feature_id`, `source_location`, `handler_type`, and `embedded_content`. All four fields are required at every `files[]` entry; absence of any field is a hard-fail at schema validation. The inventory is data-driven; the schema MUST NOT hard-code a count of files per target. The same `feature_id` MAY appear on multiple file entries within a record (one feature may contribute many files to one target).

requirement.name: feature_id validates by regex shape against the agile_backlog feature pattern
requirement.requirement: Every `files[i].feature_id` MUST validate against the regex shape declared in the schema (`^EPIC-[0-9]{3}-F-[0-9]{3}$`), which is sourced from the agile_backlog feature_id pattern at `https://dev.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyAgileBacklogSchema.json`. The schema MUST NOT enumerate which feature identifiers exist. At gate time the crosswalk validator MUST cross-reference each distinct `feature_id` appearing in any TargetRecord's `files[]` against `agile_backlog.json` and reject the instance if any `feature_id` does not resolve to a real feature node.

requirement.name: source_location is a repo-relative path with no directory-layout assumption
requirement.requirement: Every `files[i].source_location` MUST be a repo-relative path matching the path-shape regex declared in the schema (forward slashes only; no leading slash; no `..` segments; no drive letters; `maxLength: 1024`). The schema MUST NOT assume any particular directory layout for any feature, MUST NOT assume a `code/` subdirectory anywhere, and MUST NOT enumerate any specific path. At gate time the crosswalk validator MUST assert that each `source_location` resolves to a real file on disk; otherwise the gate rejects.

requirement.name: handler_type taxonomy is closed with no catchall
requirement.requirement: Every `files[i].handler_type` MUST be a member of the closed enum declared in the V18 schema: `python_source` | `python_test` | `python_requirements` | `dockerfile` | `workflow_yaml` | `shell_script` | `bat_script` | `markdown` | `json` | `static_asset` | `cert_or_key`. The taxonomy is CLOSED. No catchall value (including but not limited to `"other"`) MAY exist in the enum. A value outside the enum MUST cause schema validation to hard-fail. Adding a new handler class MUST be done by revising the schema; there is no escape hatch in the data.

requirement.name: embedded_content is required at every files[] entry; absence is a hard-fail
requirement.requirement: Every `files[i].embedded_content` MUST be present at every `files[]` entry; absence is a hard-fail at schema validation. The field MUST be a JSON string whose decoded bytes are byte-equal to the on-disk file at `files[i].source_location`. The schema MUST NOT encode any transformation, splicing, interpolation, substitution, or implicit default rule on `embedded_content`. Byte-equality is enforced by software at gate time (see check_file_drift).

requirement.name: Schema self-validates as Draft 2020-12 and the embedded example validates against it
requirement.requirement: The deployment-architecture JSON Schema MUST be JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 and MUST self-validate as such (i.e. `Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)` returns cleanly). The embedded `examples[0]` TargetRecord in the schema document MUST validate against the schema with zero errors when checked by `Draft202012Validator(schema).iter_errors(example)`. Both checks MUST run at every gate invocation that loads the schema; failure of either MUST cause the gate to reject the commit.

requirement.name: RecordLoader schema-validates every TargetRecord before return
requirement.requirement: RecordLoader MUST read the persisted collection of TargetRecord documents, validate every document against the canonical schema URL declared on the V18 schema's `$id`, and return a typed iterable whose per-document shape exposes `target_id`, `target_kind`, `environments` (a collection of EnvironmentBinding value objects), and `files` (a collection of FileComposition value objects). A schema-validation failure on any document MUST raise and abort the caller. RecordLoader MUST NOT return a partially-validated iterable. RecordLoader MUST NOT carry any soft-fail / warning path.

requirement.name: Both brain JSONs are schema-validated at every gate invocation
requirement.requirement: Every invocation of the deployment gate (commit-boundary hook and operator-invoked validator) MUST schema-validate BOTH `agile_backlog.json` AND every TargetRecord in the persisted deployment collection against their canonical published schemas BEFORE running any other check. A non-validating instance MUST cause the gate to terminate as REJECT.

requirement.name: Crosswalk gate is hard-fail-only; every finding is PASS or REJECT with no third state
requirement.requirement: The Crosswalk gate MUST resolve every finding to exactly one of two outcomes: PASS or REJECT. No third state (warning, soft-fail, advisory, retry, deferred) MAY exist anywhere on the gate path. The gate MUST NOT iterate to repair; on REJECT it halts at the point of failure. The operator returns to authoring the TargetRecord(s) before re-running the gate from the top.

requirement.name: Crosswalk runs exactly four checks beyond schema validation
requirement.requirement: Beyond the schema-validation step on both brain JSONs, Crosswalk MUST run exactly four checks: (1) REQ-to-artifact coverage (every feature node in `agile_backlog.json` whose status indicates active engineering work has at least one corresponding `files[i].feature_id` reference somewhere in the persisted collection); (2) artifact-to-REQ orphan check (no `files[i].feature_id` points at a feature absent from `agile_backlog.json`); (3) byte-equality of every on-disk artifact at `files[i].source_location` with the corresponding `files[i].embedded_content`; (4) no `.env` value appears anywhere in any TargetRecord. Each check terminates as PASS or REJECT; no other check MAY be added without a schema/design revision.

requirement.name: Reject text names the failure only; no recovery guidance is emitted
requirement.requirement: Every REJECT emitted by the deployment gate MUST be a bare single-line message of the form `REJECT - <one-line failure>` (e.g. `REJECT - file_drift between embedded_content and on-disk bytes`, `REJECT - secret VALUE present in JSON`, `REJECT - crosswalk failure on <branch tip>`). The reject text MUST name the failure only. The reject text MUST NOT contain recovery guidance, MUST NOT instruct the operator to edit any file, MUST NOT instruct the operator to run any tool, MUST NOT suggest a continuation, and MUST NOT include any soft-fail language. The reject text is fixed in code per finding; there is no configurable reject-message attribute anywhere on the gate path.

requirement.name: Crosswalk coverage check: every active backlog feature is referenced by at least one files[].feature_id
requirement.requirement: The crosswalk validator MUST assert that every feature node in `agile_backlog.json` whose status indicates active engineering work has at least one corresponding `files[i].feature_id` reference somewhere in the persisted deployment collection. A feature with zero references MUST cause the gate to REJECT. The check operates across the entire collection of TargetRecords; it does not require coverage within any single document.

requirement.name: Crosswalk orphan check: no files[].feature_id points at a non-existent feature
requirement.requirement: The crosswalk validator MUST assert that every distinct `files[i].feature_id` appearing in the persisted deployment collection resolves to a real feature node in `agile_backlog.json`. Any `feature_id` that does not resolve MUST cause the gate to REJECT with the bare-reject form (REQ-T-028).

requirement.name: check_file_drift: on-disk file byte-equals files[].embedded_content; mismatch is bare REJECT
requirement.requirement: For every row in every TargetRecord's `files[]`, Crosswalk's `check_file_drift` MUST assert that the bytes of the on-disk file at `source_location` are byte-equal to the bytes of `embedded_content`. Any mismatch MUST cause the gate to terminate as REJECT and emit `REJECT - file_drift between embedded_content and on-disk bytes`. The reject text MUST NOT contain recovery guidance; it MUST NOT instruct the operator to edit the JSON or run the extractor.

requirement.name: check_no_secret_values: no .env VALUE appears in any TargetRecord; match is bare REJECT
requirement.requirement: Crosswalk's `check_no_secret_values` MUST assert that no string anywhere in any TargetRecord (including any field inside `environments[]` or `files[]`, and including every `embedded_content` byte-equal text field) equals any value loaded from the local `.env` store. Any match MUST cause the gate to terminate as REJECT and emit `REJECT - secret VALUE present in JSON`. The check MUST NOT log the matched value. The check MUST NOT write the matched value to disk.

requirement.name: Crosswalk is the sole drift surface; Extractor MUST NOT expose detect_drift
requirement.requirement: `check_file_drift` on Crosswalk MUST be the SOLE drift-detection surface on the deploy chain. Extractor MUST NOT expose a `detect_drift` method, MUST NOT expose any per-file drift inspection, and MUST NOT return any drift findings. No other class on the deploy chain (Builder, RecordLoader, RecordWriter, SecretsResolver, PreCommitHook, local deployer) MAY implement a drift-detection surface.

requirement.name: Builder.build_record is a deliberate operator action; Builder is not a recovery surface
requirement.requirement: Builder MUST expose `build_record(target_id, repo_root) -> TargetRecord` as the SOLE entry point for constructing or refreshing a TargetRecord from the live tree. `build_record` MUST be invoked as a deliberate operator action (e.g. when a managed file is created, moved, or deleted). Builder MUST NOT expose a `refresh_files` method. Builder MUST NOT expose any auto-repair surface. Builder MUST NOT be invoked automatically by any watcher, hook, IDE save event, or extractor. Builder MUST self-validate the constructed record against the V18 schema before returning; on schema violation Builder MUST raise and the operator halts. Builder MUST NOT return a partially-validated record alongside a findings report.

requirement.name: Builder is the only writer of TargetRecord documents
requirement.requirement: Builder MUST be the only code path that constructs or refreshes a TargetRecord. RecordWriter persists what Builder produces; no other module on the deploy chain (RecordLoader, Crosswalk, Extractor, SecretsResolver, PreCommitHook, local deployer, promote workflow) MAY construct, refresh, edit, or write a TargetRecord. Out-of-band edits by hand are permitted only between Builder invocations; Crosswalk's gate catches any inconsistency before it ships.

requirement.name: Extractor.materialize writes embedded_content byte-for-byte; no retry, no repair, no soft-fail
requirement.requirement: Extractor MUST expose `materialize(record, repo_root) -> None` that writes every `files[i].embedded_content` to its `files[i].source_location` verbatim, byte-for-byte. Extractor MUST NOT apply template substitution, splicing, interpolation, or any other transformation to `embedded_content`. Extractor MUST NOT retry an I/O failure. Extractor MUST NOT attempt to repair a mismatched on-disk file. Extractor MUST NOT carry any soft-fail or warning path. Errors MUST propagate (the method raises). If Extractor requires a secret value at write time, it MUST obtain that value exclusively through SecretsResolver's public entry point.

requirement.name: SecretsResolver is the single value-fetching code path
requirement.requirement: SecretsResolver MUST be the SOLE public entry point for obtaining a secret VALUE at runtime. SecretsResolver MUST expose `resolve(name, env) -> str` as the only public method that returns a value. All file-read access to any store of secret values (local `.env`, CI store, hosting-platform store, cloud secret manager) MUST be encapsulated by private helper methods on SecretsResolver. No other module on the deploy chain (Builder, Extractor, Crosswalk, RecordLoader, RecordWriter, PreCommitHook, local deployer, promote workflow) MAY read a secret store directly. The set of `(name, env)` pairs SecretsResolver answers for MUST be sourced from `deployment_architecture.json`'s per-target per-env key declaration; no other inventory of keys may exist.

requirement.name: SecretsResolver binds each (name, env) to exactly one store; no cross-store fallback
requirement.requirement: SecretsResolver MUST carry a `bindings: dict[tuple[str, str], str]` constructor argument that maps each `(name, env)` pair to exactly one store identifier. The `bindings` argument MUST be constructed by reading the per-target per-env key declarations from `deployment_architecture.json`; no hand-built constructor binding is permitted. A private `_store_for(name, env) -> str` MUST look up the binding and raise when no binding exists for the pair. `resolve(name, env)` MUST read from the bound store ONLY. If the bound store is unavailable at resolution time, `resolve` MUST raise; it MUST NOT try another store. There is no cross-store fallback anywhere on the resolver path. Each runtime env binds to its own secret store; values never cross stores.

requirement.name: SecretsResolver never writes secret values to disk and never logs them
requirement.requirement: SecretsResolver MUST load secret VALUES into memory only. SecretsResolver MUST NOT write any secret value to disk under any circumstance. SecretsResolver MUST NOT emit any secret value to a log, console, error message, exception text, traceback, or telemetry channel. The crosswalk validator's `check_no_secret_values` (REQ-T-032) inherits these constraints when it loads values via the resolver at gate time.

requirement.name: PreCommitHook is a pure gate: on_commit(staged_files) -> int, 0=PASS / 1=REJECT
requirement.requirement: PreCommitHook MUST expose `on_commit(staged_files) -> int` as its sole entry point. The return value MUST be exactly `0` on PASS and exactly `1` on REJECT. PreCommitHook MUST be a pure gate. PreCommitHook MUST NOT auto-extract, MUST NOT auto-build, MUST NOT auto-repair, MUST NOT mutate the staged tree, MUST NOT mutate the persisted collection, and MUST NOT write to disk on its own behalf. PreCommitHook MUST NOT carry a configurable `reject_message` attribute; the reject text is fixed in code per finding (REQ-T-028).

requirement.name: Gate trigger is the git commit boundary only; no watcher, no save-time trigger
requirement.requirement: The deployment gate MUST be invoked exclusively at the `git commit` boundary by the existing pre-commit hook chain. No filesystem watcher MAY engage the gate. No IDE save-time trigger MAY engage the gate. No auto-extractor side effect MAY engage the gate. Save events, ad-hoc tooling runs, and experimentation MUST NOT engage the gate. The gate is also invokable explicitly by the operator (e.g. as a CLI), but never automatically outside the commit boundary.

requirement.name: No "configure if absent" patterns anywhere on the deploy chain
requirement.requirement: No code on the deploy chain (Builder, Extractor, Crosswalk, RecordLoader, RecordWriter, SecretsResolver, PreCommitHook, local deployer, promote workflow) MAY implement a "configure if absent" pattern. A missing TargetRecord, a missing `environments[]` entry, a missing `files[]` entry, a missing `(name, env)` binding in SecretsResolver, a missing on-disk artifact, or any other missing state MUST be treated as REJECT. The deploy chain MUST NOT synthesize defaults to paper over missing state.

requirement.name: TargetRecord value objects expose the four-key abstract tuple; no metadata field
requirement.requirement: The architecture-side typed value object MUST expose a record-level type whose fields are exactly `target_id`, `target_kind`, `environments`, and `files`; an environment-binding type whose fields are exactly `env_binding` and `node_address`; and a file-composition type whose fields are exactly `feature_id`, `source_location`, `handler_type`, and `embedded_content`. The value objects MUST NOT carry any field whose name or type encodes a business product, service, or feature, and MUST NOT carry any field named `metadata`.

requirement.name: All deploy chain code lives under architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/code/
requirement.requirement: All implementation modules for the deploy chain (Builder, Extractor, Crosswalk, RecordLoader, RecordWriter, DeploymentCollection, SecretsResolver, PreCommitHook, local deployer, and the CLI bootstrap helper) MUST live under `architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/code/`. After migration, no deploy chain code MAY live under `Code/deploy/`. The deploy chain MUST NOT assume a `code/` subdirectory inside any other feature directory.

requirement.name: Direct edit to a derived on-disk file is rejected with the bare file_drift reject
requirement.requirement: When a derived on-disk file (e.g. a workflow YAML, Dockerfile, certificate, key, or other artifact written by Extractor from `files[i].embedded_content`) is edited directly such that the staged file no longer byte-equals the corresponding TargetRecord row's `embedded_content`, PreCommitHook MUST return `1` and the gate MUST emit `REJECT - file_drift between embedded_content and on-disk bytes`. The reject text MUST NOT contain recovery guidance, MUST NOT name the offending file, MUST NOT instruct the operator to run any tool, and MUST NOT suggest a continuation.

requirement.name: Literal secret value pasted into any TargetRecord is rejected with the bare secret reject
requirement.requirement: When a literal secret value matching any value held in the local `.env` store is pasted into any string anywhere in any TargetRecord, `check_no_secret_values` MUST detect the match and PreCommitHook MUST return `1`. The gate MUST emit `REJECT - secret VALUE present in JSON`. The check MUST NOT log the matched value. The check MUST NOT emit the matched value in the reject text. The check MUST NOT write the matched value to disk.

requirement.name: Initial-load CLI bootstrap enumerates target_ids; Builder derives each TargetRecord per-target
requirement.requirement: A one-shot initial-load CLI bootstrap MUST exist that enumerates deployment targets from the live tree and emits a `target_id` list. The operator MUST then drive `Builder.build_record(target_id, repo_root)` per target_id; each invocation MUST derive `target_kind` from the closed V18 enum, enumerate `environments[]` (one entry per env_binding under which the target is realized along with its `node_address`), enumerate `files[]` (each row's `feature_id`, `source_location`, `handler_type`, and `embedded_content`), and self-validate the constructed record against the V18 schema before return. The CLI bootstrap MUST NOT read or embed any secret value. On any schema violation Builder raises and the operator halts (no retry loop, no iteration to repair).

requirement.name: Retire prior deployment source-of-truth; migrate every datum verbatim into the collection
requirement.requirement: Any prior Python source-of-truth for the deployment model (including but not limited to a hand-maintained `technical_model.py` or equivalent) and any prior single-document deployment-architecture JSON whose shape predates V18 MUST be retired. Every data element they previously held MUST move verbatim into the persisted TargetRecord collection at the canonical node dictated by the V18 schema: target-platform identity into `target_id` and `target_kind`; per-environment addressing into `environments[].env_binding` and `environments[].node_address`; per-feature file composition into `files[].feature_id`, `files[].source_location`, `files[].handler_type`, and `files[].embedded_content`. No `metadata` field MAY be carried forward; record-level provenance is NOT part of the V18 shape and MUST instead be tracked out-of-band (e.g. in commit metadata or audit-log streams) by software, not by the schema.

requirement.name: One local + one remote deploy script pair (symmetric)
requirement.requirement: The deploy toolchain MUST consist of exactly two operator-facing local scripts (`local_build.py`, `local_deploy.py`) and exactly two CI-facing remote scripts (`remote_build.py`, `remote_deploy.py`). No other script MAY exist on the deploy chain. The two pairs are symmetric: each `build` produces a versioned per-target package; the paired `deploy` ships that package to its target. Adding a script outside this four-way symmetry MUST cause the gate to REJECT.

requirement.name: Code-branch facts live in deployment_architecture.json
requirement.requirement: Every TargetRecord whose `target_kind` resolves to a git-branch-bound cloud destination MUST declare the source code branch as a fact in `environments[].node_address` (or an equivalent typed field reachable from the manifest). The build and deploy scripts MUST read the branch from the manifest and MUST NOT carry a hard-coded branch map anywhere in code.

requirement.name: Local-build source directories live in deployment_architecture.json
requirement.requirement: Every TargetRecord whose `target_kind` requires materialized local source for the build MUST declare every contributing source path in `files[].source_location`. `local_build.py` MUST read source bytes ONLY from local-disk paths declared in the manifest. No remote fetch of source bytes (git remote, HTTP, registry pull, etc.) is permitted during `local_build`; any such call MUST cause the build to REJECT.

requirement.name: Per-target `secrets` map declares secret/env-key NAMES and store bindings
requirement.requirement: Every TargetRecord MAY carry a `secrets` map of `name -> store_id`. Each entry names a secret or environment key the target requires at runtime and binds it to exactly one store from the closed enum: `local_env` | `gha_secret` | `hf_space_secret` | `cloudflare_env` | `azure_function_app_setting` | `azure_automation_variable`. Secret VALUES MUST NEVER appear in the manifest. SecretsResolver bindings (per REQ-T-038) MUST be constructed by reading these declarations; no other inventory of (name, store) pairs may exist on the deploy chain.

requirement.name: Build packages contain no secret VALUES
requirement.requirement: No file inside any per-target build-package directory under `local_build/v{N}/<target_id>/` or `remote_build/v{N}/<target_id>/` MAY contain any secret VALUE held in any bound secrets store (operator `.env`, GHA secrets, HF Space secrets, Cloudflare env, Azure Function App settings, Azure Automation Variables). The build MUST emit only (a) the per-target manifest snapshot declaring secret NAMES + store bindings and (b) the source bytes needed by the deploy. The pre-commit gate MUST scan every staged build-package file and REJECT on any matched value.

requirement.name: Versioned build packages tracked in git
requirement.requirement: `local_build` MUST emit per-target packages under `architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/local_build/v{N}/<target_id>/` and `remote_build` MUST emit them under the matching `remote_build/v{N}/<target_id>/`. Each package directory MUST be tracked in git (no gitignore exemption). `N` is the system-wide build counter read from `admin.Versions` on the front-end cluster `chathealthyfrontend` (per REQ-T-002 / REQ-T-003), so the git history carries exactly one versioned tree per system release.

requirement.name: All builds run on a local workstation or a named CI runner; never elsewhere
requirement.requirement: Every build action MUST execute either on the operator's local workstation (`local_build.py`) or on a named GitHub Actions runner (`remote_build.py`). No build action MAY execute on a deploy target, a customer-facing host, an HF Space, an Azure Function App, a Cloudflare worker, or any other environment outside the two named build contexts. The build chain MUST hard-fail if invoked outside these two contexts.

requirement.name: Deploy script is accountable to install, configure, and component-build at deploy time
requirement.requirement: `local_deploy.py` and `remote_deploy.py` MUST be the SINGLE accountable entry points for getting a target from its build package into its running state. For each target the deploy script MUST: read the package manifest under `local_build/v{N}/<target_id>/` or `remote_build/v{N}/<target_id>/`; install the package on its target; configure the target's runtime environment (env vars / secrets / app settings) by resolving each declared `secrets` binding via SecretsResolver against the bound store; and build any deploy-time-built components the target requires (docker image, zip, container, etc.). No post-deploy step outside the deploy script may exist.

story.name: Local-only deploy
story.description: What is unique to deploying on the developer's workstation. Backend services run as local Docker containers per the port table (S-001-REQ-T-001). MongoDB connections target the dev front-end cluster — the only resource shared with dev. The Website wrapper, which binds privileged ports 80 and 443, runs as a host-OS process (Docker exception). All other deploy facts live in S-001 and S-003.

requirement.name: Backend containers
requirement.requirement: All three backend services (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) run as local Docker containers built from each backend's Dockerfile and requirements.txt. The local runtime MUST NOT import any Python package not installed by the container's pip install. Ports per S-001-REQ-T-001.

requirement.name: Local Host WebSite must run from within Local docker image
requirement.requirement: Local Host WebSite must run from within Local docker image. No other requirement is waived because of this requirement.

requirement.name: Shared dev MongoDB
requirement.requirement: When deploying locally, all backend services connect to the dev front-end MongoDB cluster (cluster `chathealthyfrontend`, database `dev_*`). This is the only resource shared between local and dev. All other state, services, and ports are local.

requirement.name: 'deployment_architecture.json' and the project's '.env' (for secrets) file is the single source of truth for all deployment facts
requirement.requirement: Local-runtime deployer reads ports table, container list, and file-system paths from the typed TargetRecord collection loaded by RecordLoader at runtime. The deployer MUST navigate the collection's target-keyed shape (filter records by `target_kind`; read the entry in `environments[]` whose `env_binding` matches `local` for the addressable node; iterate `files[]` for source-file composition) rather than any flat lookup. The deployer MUST NOT carry any hardcoded ports dict, container dict, or path constant in source. All facts necessary to build, deploy assets to, or describe a server in the ChatHealthy digital portfolio must reside only in the local .env file or the single source of truth for these facts. Any constant previously embedded in source that drives deploy behavior MUST move into the appropriate TargetRecord verbatim. After migration, no port number, container name, or file-system path that drives local deploy behavior MAY appear as a literal in any resource other than the Brain file, 'deployment_architecture.json'. If it is necessary to construct YAML, DOCKER, or other files in order to accomplish a build or deployment to a server, those assets MUST be built during the primary script's execution and deleted as soon as possible after being transmitted to the nodes that need them.

requirement.name: Local deployer binds local-env secrets via SecretsResolver only; no cross-store fallback
requirement.requirement: When the local-runtime deployer requires a secret VALUE (e.g. to start a local container with the local-env binding), it MUST obtain that value exclusively through `SecretsResolver.resolve(name, env='local')`. The local-env binding MUST resolve to the local `.env` store only; no other store MAY be queried, and no cross-store fallback MAY be attempted. If the bound store is unavailable, SecretsResolver raises and the local deployer halts; the deployer MUST NOT continue with a default, an empty value, or a value sourced from a different env.

requirement.name: Local deployer halts on any missing-state condition; no "configure if absent" path
requirement.requirement: If the TargetRecord collection at runtime does not contain a `target_kind` the deployer needs, a `local` entry in `environments[]` for a target the deployer is starting, a required `(name, 'local')` binding in SecretsResolver, or a required `files[]` row on disk, the deployer MUST halt with a non-zero exit and the bare-reject form (REQ-T-028). The deployer MUST NOT synthesize a default port, default path, default container name, or default secret value to paper over missing state.

requirement.name: Every deployed service runs in its own Docker container; deploy tooling via automation
requirement.requirement: Every deployed service of the Local environment (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices, the Website wrapper) runs inside its own Docker container per REQ-T-007 / REQ-T-008. The deploy tooling of the ChatHealthy.ai front-end components all must be deployed via automation.

requirement.name: Single Docker engine on the workstation
requirement.requirement: The Local environment runs in a single Docker engine instance on the operator's workstation. The engine is Docker Desktop on Windows / macOS or Docker Engine on Linux. No Kubernetes orchestrator, no Docker Swarm, no second engine instance. All containers enumerated in REQ-T-007 MUST run inside this one engine.

requirement.name: Five containers managed by local_deploy
requirement.requirement: local_deploy.py MUST teardown and re-launch exactly five Docker containers per invocation: the three backend service containers (ch-findcare, ch-evalcare, ch-sharedsvc) per REQ-T-001, the Website wrapper container per REQ-T-002, and the Kafka container. No container is treated as "separate infrastructure"; all five live under the same Docker engine (REQ-T-006) and the same atomic deploy lifecycle (S-001-REQ-B-001).

requirement.name: One Dockerfile per container
requirement.requirement: Each of the five containers in REQ-T-007 MUST be built from its own dedicated Dockerfile checked into the repo. No two containers share a Dockerfile. No container runs more than one of the named services (i.e., no multi-process container hosting two backends, or a backend and the Website, or the Website and Kafka).

story.name: Deployed-env deploy (dev/qa/prod)
story.description: What is unique to deploying to the dev, qa, or prod environments. A single script accepts the environment as parameter and pushes to the matching HuggingFace paid Space (Docker, lowest tier) via GitHub Actions. Cloudflare Pages serves the static chathealthy.ai site for these envs.

requirement.name: Single parameterized script
requirement.requirement: One deploy script accepts an environment parameter (dev | qa | prod) and pushes to the corresponding HuggingFace paid Space. Logic is identical across the three environments except for prod-only behaviors (S-004) and the absence of non-prod display chrome (S-005) in prod.

requirement.name: Deployments come from correct Code branches and file location
requirement.requirement: Local deployments must come from the local file system. Dev must come from the committed and pushed dev branch of the GitHub repository. QA must come from the committed and pushed QA branch of the repository. Production must come from the head of main.

requirement.name: HuggingFace README preservation
requirement.requirement: Every HuggingFace Space deploy preserves the target Space's README.md across the push. README.md carries the HF Space frontmatter configuration (sdk, python_version, license) and MUST NOT be wiped. Missing README.md after a deploy is a violation.

requirement.name: Cloudflare HTTP→HTTPS
requirement.requirement: Every Cloudflare Pages deployment of chathealthy.ai (dev, qa, prod) 301-redirects every http:// request to its https:// equivalent. The redirect is immediate (no intermediate response, no caching delay) and applies to every path. The deploy script MUST verify this setting and configure it if absent.

requirement.name: Cloudflare 404 error page
requirement.requirement: Cloudflare Pages returns HTTP 404 for unknown paths and renders a dedicated error page (not a blank response, not a redirect, not the home page). CloudFlare's default convention of redirecting unknown paths to the site root MUST be explicitly disabled. The deploy script verifies this setting and configures it if absent.

requirement.name: promote-build.yml invokes Crosswalk on the source-branch tip before merging; each step is an explicit operator action
requirement.requirement: `promote-build.yml` MUST invoke Crosswalk (full check: schema-validation of both brain JSONs; REQ-to-artifact coverage; artifact-to-REQ orphan check; byte-equality of every `files[i].embedded_content` against its on-disk `source_location`; no `.env` value anywhere in the collection) on the source-branch tip before any merge into the target branch. Both branches of the alt block MUST be explicit: on PASS the workflow proceeds to merge; on REJECT the workflow MUST exit 1 with the bare-reject form `REJECT - crosswalk failure on <tip>` and halt; no merge MAY occur, no Mongo write MAY occur. Each promotion step (dev to qa, qa to main) MUST be an independently triggered explicit operator action; the chain MUST NOT auto-progress past one step into the next.

requirement.name: promote-build.yml writes admin.Versions builds[<env>].build only after Crosswalk PASS
requirement.requirement: On the dev-to-qa step, after Crosswalk on the dev tip terminates as PASS, `promote-build.yml` MUST merge dev into qa and write `builds[qa].build = builds[dev].build` into `admin.Versions`. On the qa-to-main step, after Crosswalk on the qa tip terminates as PASS, the workflow MUST merge qa into main and write `builds[prod].build = builds[dev].build` per the existing per-env build-counter semantic. On REJECT at either step, the workflow MUST NOT merge and MUST NOT write to `admin.Versions`.

requirement.name: Each runtime env binds to its own secret store; values never cross stores
requirement.requirement: Each runtime `env_binding` (`local`, `dev`, `qa`, `prod`) MUST bind to its own secret store at SecretsResolver construction time. The promote-build chain MUST NOT copy a value from one env's store into another env's store. The promote-build chain MUST NOT resolve a secret value for one env and use it under another env_binding. SecretsResolver's `resolve(name, env)` MUST raise if the bound store for the requested `(name, env)` pair is unavailable; no cross-store fallback MAY be attempted by the promote workflow or any other deploy-chain consumer.

requirement.name: 'deployment_architecture.json' and the project's '.env' (for secrets) file is the single source of truth for all deployment facts
requirement.requirement: Deployed-env deployer reads ports table, container list, and file-system paths from the typed TargetRecord collection loaded by RecordLoader at runtime. The deployer MUST navigate the collection's target-keyed shape (filter records by `target_kind`; read the entry in `environments[]` whose `env_binding` matches the target environment — `dev`, `qa`, or `prod` — for the addressable node; iterate `files[]` for source-file composition) rather than any flat lookup. The deployer MUST NOT carry any hardcoded ports dict, container dict, or path constant in source. All facts necessary to build, deploy assets to, or describe a server in the ChatHealthy digital portfolio must reside only in the local .env file or the single source of truth for these facts. Any constant previously embedded in source that drives deploy behavior MUST move into the appropriate TargetRecord verbatim. After migration, no port number, container name, or file-system path that drives deployed-env deploy behavior MAY appear as a literal in any resource other than the Brain file, 'deployment_architecture.json'. If it is necessary to construct YAML, DOCKER, or other files in order to accomplish a build or deployment to a server, those assets MUST be built during the primary script's execution and deleted as soon as possible after being transmitted to the nodes that need them.

story.name: Prod-only behaviors
story.description: The only differences between prod and the dev/qa environments, aside from their different addresses, are: (1) the chrome banner with versions and navigation between the servers does not appear in prod, and (2) the security GUI widget does not appear in prod.

requirement.name: Version & framework ID assignment
requirement.requirement: When environment=prod, after human UAT sign-off, the deploy script accepts human-supplied values for a new version ID (and potentially a new framework ID) and writes them to the version document (per S-001-REQ-T-002). Dev and qa deploys never change these fields. No automation, ever, sets version or framework.

requirement.name: Display chrome OFF
requirement.requirement: In prod, the non-prod display chrome (S-005) MUST NOT render: no environment banner, no security token panel, no service-switching buttons. The smoke test (S-006) skips display-chrome checks when env=prod via its macro-variance dimension.

story.name: Non-prod display chrome
story.description: Display chrome visible in local, dev, and qa; absent in prod (see S-004-REQ-B-002). Owns the environment banner, the security-token panel, and the three service-switching buttons. Banner reads /health from whichever service currently owns the page (FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices).

requirement.name: Banner contents
requirement.requirement: The environment banner displays environment label (LOCAL/DEV/QA), version, framework, and build, fetched from the /health endpoint of whichever service currently owns the page. All values render on one line with sufficient spacing for human readability. The banner displays the active service name in brackets (e.g., [evaluatecare]).

requirement.name: Banner re-fetches on ownership transfer
requirement.requirement: When page ownership transfers between services, the banner re-fetches /health from the new owner and updates inline.

requirement.name: Service buttons + active is cold
requirement.requirement: Three service-switching buttons (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) appear in the banner. The currently-active service's button is cold (greyed, disabled); on click it shows tooltip 'You are here already'. The other two buttons are hot (clickable, styled). Clicking a hot button transfers page ownership to that service, which then controls the entire frame. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

requirement.name: Unimplemented placeholder
requirement.requirement: The center panel displays the service name and 'is still unimplemented.' when SharedServices or EvaluateCare has control, until those services have real implementations. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

requirement.name: Security token panel
requirement.requirement: Each service displays a security token panel rendered per the mock at {projectRoot}/brain/machine_artifacts/diagramsAndImages/GUIImagesAndMockUps/NonProdSecuriytToken.jpg. Right panel and lower regions display the security information defined by EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-007. The content of this display must be served by the HuggingFace server that owns the content.

story.name: Smoke test
story.description: One master Playwright pytest (`Code/deploy/localSmokeTestPyTest.py`) runs against any environment. The script varies along three dimensions: (1) environment — localhost / dev / qa / prod; (2) macro variance — display chrome (banner, token, service buttons) is exercised in non-prod and skipped in prod per S-004-REQ-B-002; (3) micro variance — PKI certificates differ across environments and the cert-verification step asserts the env-appropriate cert is in use. The actual script is the source of truth: where these requirements differ from the script's behavior, the script wins and these requirements MUST be reverse-engineered to match. Per-step requirements below (REQ-B-002 through REQ-B-037) capture each test class in the script.

requirement.name: Master smoke-test contract
requirement.requirement: `localSmokeTestPyTest.py` is the single master smoke test. It accepts the target environment as a parameter and exercises every step below in declared order. Every step MUST pass for the smoke test to PASS overall.

requirement.name: Step 00 — Build gate: local and dev report identical build
requirement.requirement: Smoke test fetches /health from local FindCare and dev FindCare and asserts the `build` field matches across the two envs. Two environments on the same build MUST be running identical code and configuration; mismatched builds halt the smoke test before any further steps.

requirement.name: Step 01 — HTTP→HTTPS redirect
requirement.requirement: Browser navigation to http://{domain} MUST 301-redirect to https://{domain}. The smoke test deliberately probes the insecure scheme (constructed at runtime) and asserts the final URL is https://.

requirement.name: Step 02 — Banner shows env label, version, framework, build
requirement.requirement: The environment banner element (`#envBanner`) MUST be visible and contain the env label (LOCAL/DEV/QA), and the literal strings `Version: <v>`, `Framework: <f>`, `Build: <b>` whose values match the response from the active service's /health.

requirement.name: Step 03 — SharedServices button is a banner button
requirement.requirement: A `<button>` with `data-service='sharedservices'` MUST exist inside `#envBanner` (not in any header nav), MUST be visible, and its label MUST be `SharedServices` (PascalCase, no space).

requirement.name: Step 04 — Splash renders welcome words
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe loads. The first 10 words of the canonical welcome message (per `_get_welcome_words`) MUST appear in the iframe body text.

requirement.name: Step 05 — Chat input enabled and focused on click
requirement.requirement: The chat input element (`input[placeholder*='Type a message']` or textarea) MUST be visible, MUST NOT carry a `disabled` attribute, and MUST become focused when clicked.

requirement.name: Step 06 — Search returns providers
requirement.requirement: Submitting `Find me a bone doctor in Delaware` MUST yield results containing NPI strings (`NPI[:\s]+\d{10}`) in the iframe body within the chat timeout. The smoke test captures the originating session token for downstream nonce comparisons.

requirement.name: Step 07 — Specialty checkboxes appear in left panel
requirement.requirement: After a search, `#leftPanel` MUST contain at least one `input[type='checkbox']` representing a specialty.

requirement.name: Step 08 — Left panel cell layout and scroll cap
requirement.requirement: The left panel MUST contain exactly four `[data-cell]` cells (1..4) with reactive percentage heights 18/40/20/22 (declared via `flex:0 0 N%` or `height:N%` — pixel heights are forbidden). An Uncheck All / Check All toggle MUST live inside cell 1 (the green header). With more than 12 prescribers present, no more than 12 specialty checkboxes may be visible in cell 2 without scrolling.

requirement.name: Step 09 — Provider NPIs in center frame
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe body MUST contain provider NPI strings (`NPI[:\s]+\d{10}`) after the search resolves.

requirement.name: Step 10 — Bottom panel zero before selection
requirement.requirement: The chat iframe body MUST contain `0 / 5` (or `0/5`) reflecting an empty Selected for Evaluation panel before any provider is selected.

requirement.name: Step 11 — Select up to three providers
requirement.requirement: Up to three provider Select-for-Evaluation buttons MUST be clickable; the smoke test clicks min(count, 3) of them.

requirement.name: Step 12 — Selected providers appear in bottom panel
requirement.requirement: After selection, the iframe body MUST include the words `SELECTED` and `EVALUATION` and the count must read 1..5 / 5 (no longer 0).

requirement.name: Step 13 — Evaluate button click
requirement.requirement: An Evaluate button (`#guiEvalBtn` or text-matched `Evaluate`) MUST be present and clickable; the smoke test clicks it to trigger handoff to EvaluateCare.

requirement.name: Step 14 — EvaluateCare has frame control
requirement.requirement: After the Evaluate click, the chat iframe (`#coreChatFrame`) MUST be hidden and `#evalcareSplash` MUST be visible — EvaluateCare owns the frame.

requirement.name: Step 15 — mTLS to EvaluateCare TLS 1.2+

requirement.name: Downstream artifacts on disk are never authored by hand; Extractor is the sole writer

requirement.name: Local Code Repository Management retires Code/deploy/ in favor of architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/code/

The crosswalk validator's coverage check MUST be re-run after the move; any stale path MUST cause REJECT.

requirement.name: File-system level rename or move of a managed file requires a deliberate Builder.build_record invocation
requirement.requirement: When the operator renames or moves a file that is referenced by `files[i].source_location` in any TargetRecord, the affected TargetRecord(s) MUST be refreshed by a deliberate `Builder.build_record(target_id, repo_root)` invocation per-target. No watcher, no IDE save event, and no auto-extractor side effect MAY refresh a TargetRecord in response to a filesystem event. If the operator commits without running Builder, Crosswalk's `check_file_drift` (REQ-T-031) MUST detect the divergence at the commit boundary and PreCommitHook MUST return `1` with the bare-reject form (REQ-T-028).

feature.name: Conversation-log Pipeline (Claude Code hooks -> Kafka -> MongoDB)
feature.description: DevOps feature that owns the end-to-end pipeline by which every Claude Code and Claude utterance is recorded. Each UserPromptSubmit and Stop hook events are persisted to long-term storage in the Mongo Db. The pipeline has three runtime components: (a) a hook-driven publisher worker that POSTs the raw hook payload to a local producer sidecar, (b) the producer sidecar HTTP service on 127.0.0.1:8100 that forwards to the conversation_log Kafka topic, and (c) a consumer that drains the topic and persists each message to MongoDB ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive. Rule-001 in engineering_rules.json is the runtime enforcement vehicle for the publisher leg of this feature.

story.name: Publisher leg - hook-driven POST to local sidecar with browser-popup failure signaling
story.description: Per-hook-event publication of the raw payload from Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks to the local producer sidecar at http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce. On sidecar unreachability the publisher MUST signal the operator visibly via a fullscreen browser warning page so the operator is never silently disconnected from the archive. This story is the implementation home for the three Rule-001 statements; Rule-001 itself is the engineering-rules vehicle that wires the worker into the hook framework.

requirement.name: UserPromptSubmit hook publishes raw payload to local producer sidecar
requirement.requirement: On every Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook event, the conversation-log publisher worker MUST read the raw hook payload from stdin and POST the unmodified JSON body to http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce with Content-Type: application/json and a request header X-Hook-Event identifying the hook event name. The POST MUST complete within the hook's configured timeout (15 seconds per Rule-001-ENF-001). A 2xx response from the sidecar is the success criterion; the worker MUST exit 0 on success.

requirement.name: Stop hook publishes raw payload to local producer sidecar
requirement.requirement: On every Claude Code Stop hook event, the conversation-log publisher worker MUST read the raw hook payload from stdin and POST the unmodified JSON body to http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce with Content-Type: application/json and X-Hook-Event identifying the hook event name. The POST MUST complete within the hook's configured timeout (15 seconds per Rule-001-ENF-002). A 2xx response is the success criterion; the worker MUST exit 0 on success.

requirement.name: Sidecar-unreachable failure shows fullscreen browser warning page to the operator
requirement.requirement: If the POST to http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce fails for any reason (connection refused, timeout, non-2xx response, OSError), the worker MUST write a viewport-filling HTML failure page to a temp-directory file and launch the operator's default browser pointed at that file. The page MUST state in unmistakable language that the conversation-log pipeline is DOWN, that Claude Code interactions are NOT being persisted, and that the operator must restart the producer sidecar. The worker MUST exit non-zero on this path so the failure surfaces in the hook's telemetry.

requirement.name: Publisher worker is wired via engineering_rules.json (Rule-001), not directly in settings.json
requirement.requirement: The conversation_log_publisher_worker.py worker MUST be invoked via the V19 engineering-rules enforcement architecture: Rule-001 declares two enforcement entries (Rule-001-ENF-001 for UserPromptSubmit, Rule-001-ENF-002 for Stop) whose executable_path points at the worker. .claude/settings.json registers the UserPromptSubmit and Stop hook commands as chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py --hook <hook> only. The settings.json file MUST NOT call the worker directly, and the worker MUST NOT be invoked by any legacy dispatch path (governance_matrix.json or chathealthy_devops_boot.py's removed conversation_log_worker class).

story.name: Producer sidecar - local HTTP service on 127.0.0.1:8100 forwarding to Kafka topic
story.description: The local producer sidecar is an HTTP service bound to 127.0.0.1:8100 that accepts POST /produce, treats the request body as an opaque JSON payload, and forwards it to the conversation_log Kafka topic. The sidecar isolates the publisher worker from Kafka client configuration, transport credentials, and broker addressing - the worker speaks plain HTTP and the sidecar speaks Kafka. Implementation lives at Code/Shared/ops/ChatHealthyLogService/.

requirement.name: Sidecar binds only to loopback at 127.0.0.1:8100 and accepts POST /produce
requirement.requirement: The producer sidecar MUST bind only to 127.0.0.1 (loopback) on TCP port 8100 and MUST NOT bind to any externally-routable interface. It MUST accept HTTP POST on path /produce with Content-Type: application/json, treating the request body as an opaque JSON payload to be forwarded unchanged to the conversation_log Kafka topic. It MUST respond with HTTP 2xx on successful produce and HTTP 5xx (or connection refusal) on any failure to forward.

requirement.name: Sidecar forwards the request body unchanged to the conversation_log Kafka topic
requirement.requirement: The producer sidecar MUST publish the request body to the Kafka topic named 'conversation_log' without modification. The sidecar MUST NOT add, remove, reorder, or otherwise mutate any fields of the JSON payload. The hook event identifier carried in the X-Hook-Event request header MAY be propagated as a Kafka message header but MUST NOT be merged into the payload body.

story.name: Consumer leg - drain conversation_log topic to MongoDB ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive
story.description: The conversation_log consumer drains the conversation_log Kafka topic and persists each message as one document to MongoDB cluster ClaudeCodeLog, collection conversation_log_archive. The consumer is the durability boundary for the pipeline - once a message is committed to the archive collection, it is considered persisted for forensic and operator-review purposes.

requirement.name: Consumer persists each Kafka message as one document in conversation_log_archive
requirement.requirement: The conversation_log consumer MUST consume the conversation_log Kafka topic and insert each message as exactly one document into MongoDB collection ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive. The consumer MUST NOT drop, merge, or batch-rewrite messages. It MUST acknowledge each Kafka offset only after the MongoDB insert returns success so an at-least-once delivery property holds across consumer restarts.

requirement.name: Consumer transforms malformed Kafka messages so every utterance lands in conversation_log_archive
requirement.requirement: The conversation_log consumer MUST treat every Kafka message as durable and MUST NOT reject or discard a message because the payload is malformed. For each message consumed from the conversation_log topic, the consumer MUST produce exactly one document in MongoDB collection ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive. When the payload is not valid JSON, when required fields (for example actor or content) are missing, when bytes are not valid UTF-8, or when content is not a string, the consumer MUST wrap, coerce, or annotate the record so that an insert_many call against the archive collection succeeds. The transformed document MUST carry a cleanup-description field that names the transformation applied (for example raw-bytes-wrapped, json-parse-failed, actor-defaulted, content-coerced-to-string). Legibility of the utterance MUST be degraded as little as possible by the transformation; loss of the utterance is forbidden. When a record fails to be written for any reason an operational response is demanded. And Rule-002 statement #5 brings this failure to the attention of a human operator.

requirement.name: Consumer redacts credentials with model-based redaction; retries on failure; stores unredacted on final failure with a pointer to the error file
requirement.requirement: Before inserting a record into ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive, the conversation_log consumer MUST submit the content field to a model-based credentials-redaction step (not regex). The redaction step MUST replace API keys, passwords, connection strings, tokens, secrets, and credentials with the literal marker [Sensitive content redacted] and MUST leave all other text exactly as-is. The redaction engine MUST be an LLM call (currently gpt-4.1-mini). The LLM system prompt MUST include the project's Code/.env file as a non-exhaustive reference (the sensitive term might not be in .env). The LLM user prompt MUST include the last 5 utterances prior to the current utterance, queried from ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive by descending timestamp_utc, so the model can contextualize what a secret might be. The consumer MUST retry the LLM call up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1s, 2s). After 3 attempts have all failed, the consumer MUST store the ORIGINAL unredacted content (durability of REQ-T-001 takes precedence over redaction success). On final failure, the consumer MUST append one JSONL line of the form {"timestamp_utc": "...", "mongo_id": "<inserted_id>", "error": "<terse cause>"} to the consumer error file at %TEMP%/chathealthy_consumer_errors.log, capturing the ObjectId returned by the Mongo insert so the failed record can be located operationally.

requirement.name: Consumer redacts profanity in content via model-based redaction with fail-open fallback
requirement.requirement: Before inserting a record into ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive, the conversation_log consumer MUST submit the content field to a model-based profanity-redaction step (not regex). The redaction step MUST replace profanity and vulgar language with the literal marker [expletive deleted] and MUST leave all other text exactly as-is. The redaction engine MUST be an LLM call (currently gpt-4.1-mini). The redaction MUST be a single attempt with no retries. If the redaction call fails or returns an error, the consumer MUST fall back to storing the unredacted content rather than dropping the message; the durability obligation of REQ-T-001 takes precedence over redaction success. Profanity redaction MUST run AFTER credentials redaction, so that if credentials redaction substituted any markers, profanity redaction operates on the already-credentials-handled content.

story.name: Pipeline cluster indexes specification

story.description: Every enrichment step (Pass 1-6) must accept and apply the states filter from the job config. No step should process records outside the specified states.

requirement.name: states parameter required on every pipeline step that touches the providers collection

requirement.name: states=["ALL"] is the sentinel for full load
