depends_on.reason: Auto-pause is implemented by ClusterLifecycleManager.release(); REQ-B-002 mandates the business outcome that S-015 delivers.

requirement.name: Durable activity fan-out runs on the Flex Consumption 'durable' per-function scale group
requirement.requirement: The Pipeline Function App MUST run on Azure Functions Flex Consumption (Linux). The provider_worker_activity Durable Functions activity MUST be hosted in the 'durable' per-function scale group as defined by Flex Consumption per-function scaling (see Microsoft Learn 'Per-function scaling' table — Durable orchestration/activity/entity triggers all map to the 'durable' settings value). When the orchestrator fans out to N partitions, the platform MUST instantiate N independent Flex Consumption instances within one full propagation interval (default ceiling: 60 seconds). Verification: a single end-to-end run at N=32 records exactly 32 distinct WEBSITE_INSTANCE_ID values across the provider_worker_activity Application Insights traces in that run.

requirement.name: Pre-warm via Managed Identity PATCH targets the correct Flex Consumption alwaysReady group
requirement.requirement: Before fan-out, the orchestrator MUST PATCH properties.functionAppConfig.scaleAndConcurrency.alwaysReady on the Flex Consumption Function App via the Azure Resource Manager API using the Function App's system-assigned Managed Identity (Website Contributor role on the site itself). The 'name' field in the alwaysReady array MUST be 'durable' (the Flex Consumption per-function scale group containing all Durable Functions triggers per Microsoft Learn), NOT a named-function value such as 'provider_worker_activity'. After fan-out completes, alwaysReady MUST be PATCHed back to [] so no always-ready baseline is billed between runs. Verification: an integration smoke test asserts the JSON body of both PATCH requests has name=='durable' and that the post-run state has alwaysReady==[]. This REQ-T directly fixes the silent no-op currently in pipeline/Code/instance_warmer.py.

depends_on.reason: Builds on REQ-T-001's Flex Consumption + 'durable' scale-group selection.

requirement.name: Durable orchestration completes within the 2-hour Function App ceiling
requirement.requirement: host.json MUST keep functionTimeout set to 02:00:00 for the Pipeline Function App. The end-to-end findcare_pipeline_orchestrator MUST complete (status=Completed) within 2 hours of orchestrator start as recorded in the Durable Task Hub instance store. Verification: a CI smoke test against a representative state-scoped load (e.g. states=['DE'], the existing dev fixture) asserts (completedTime - createdTime) <= 7200 seconds; a periodic prod assertion does the same against the most recent successful run for the next-largest state cohort approved by Skip.

depends_on.reason: The 2-h ceiling is achievable only with the fan-out scaling fix in REQ-T-001 + REQ-T-002.

requirement.name: Zero always-ready baseline + Atlas paused between runs (live-state assertion)
requirement.requirement: Between Pipeline runs the system MUST hold (a) the Flex Consumption Function App with zero always-ready instances configured (Microsoft Learn: Flex Consumption apps that scale to zero, or instances marked to scale in and delete, do not count against the quota; in on-demand mode no minimum instance count is required); and (b) the MongoDB Atlas pipeline cluster ChatHealthyDataPipelines in PAUSED state via the existing ClusterLifecycleManager release path. Verification: a daily Azure Function timer (already present in function_app.py as cluster_lifecycle_timer) MUST additionally read the Function App's scaleAndConcurrency.alwaysReady and assert it is []; the same timer MUST read the LIVE cluster_lifecycle document and assert that when the count of currently-active reservations is zero, the Atlas cluster stateName is PAUSED. The assertion is point-in-time against the live document only — no historical aggregation, no released/orphan rows examined (none exist under live-only). Discrepancies fire the existing pipeline_health alert path.

depends_on.reason: Depends on REQ-T-002 PATCH-back-to-[] behavior and on REQ-T-008's live-only data-store rule.

requirement.name: Azure Cost Management budget caps non-storage Pipeline spend with action-group alerting
requirement.requirement: An Azure Cost Management budget MUST exist on the Pipeline subscription scoped to resource tag workload=findcare-pipeline (so storage accounts holding NPPES blobs can be excluded by counter-tag and remain unconstrained per Skip's storage-cost exception). The budget MUST be set to the per-month spend Skip approves and MUST have at least two threshold rules (e.g. 50%, 90%) wired to an Azure Monitor action group whose webhook hits the existing pipeline_health.send_admin_notification SparkPost path. Verification: deployment of the Bicep template results in the budget resource present in 'az consumption budget list', and a synthetic forced-breach (set threshold to $0.01 in dev) generates an email within 24 hours. Note: per Microsoft Learn budgets evaluate every 12-14 hours and don't support a daily time grain — alert is detection, not real-time prevention.

requirement.name: Per-instance memory size sufficient for NPPES partition processing
requirement.requirement: The Flex Consumption instance memory size for the Pipeline Function App MUST be set to 4096 MB (the 2 vCPU SKU per Microsoft Learn 'Instance sizes' table). Justification: each provider_worker_activity replica streams a ~265 MB / ~8.85M-row CSV partition through PyMongo bulk_write to Atlas; 2048 MB instances were observed to OOM (exit code 137) under stacked-worker conditions. Verification: the Bicep template MUST declare properties.functionAppConfig.scaleAndConcurrency.instanceMemoryMB = 4096, and a CI assertion against 'az functionapp show' MUST fail if any environment drifts off 4096.

depends_on.reason: Sized for the per-replica workload established by REQ-T-001's fan-out model.

requirement.name: Reservation data store is live-only; no in-application history
requirement.requirement: The Pipeline cluster reservation data store ({env}_System.cluster_lifecycle on the ChatHealthyDataPipelines Atlas cluster) MUST hold only currently-live reservations. ClusterLifecycleManager.release() MUST remove the released row from the document; it MUST NOT transition a status field, MUST NOT write a release_time history field, and MUST NOT preserve the row. The 5-minute overdue reaper MUST delete overdue automated rows (it MUST NOT tag them with a status='orphan' value). The document MUST NOT carry a TTL index for reservation history because no history is retained. Forensic and audit needs (who reserved what, when, with what outcome) are served by three external platform sinks and only by those sinks: (1) MongoDB Atlas database auditing on the ChatHealthyDataPipelines project, which records every insert/update/delete against the cluster_lifecycle collection in Atlas's native audit log; (2) Azure Activity Log on the Pipeline subscription, which records every control-plane operation against the Function App and Atlas-related Azure resources; (3) Application Insights and the Azure Monitor Log Analytics workspace receiving Function App diagnostic settings, which capture orchestrator and activity-function traces for every run. Verification: a CI assertion reads the cluster_lifecycle document after a synthetic release() call and asserts the released job_id is absent from the live array. A second CI assertion confirms there is no TTL index named on release_time/reap_time on the collection. A documentation assertion confirms Atlas database auditing is enabled on the project and that the Function App's diagnostic settings ship to the Log Analytics workspace declared in Bicep.

story.name: All Azure changes are scripted; no ad hoc admin outside Development
story.description: Every Azure change — both resource provisioning and code deployment — happens through scripts. Operator portal-clicks and CLI hand-edits are prohibited in QA and Production. Scripts are authored and proven in Development before being used elsewhere.

requirement.name: Scripted deployments only; ad hoc administration limited to Development
requirement.requirement: All deployments to Azure, including the provisioning of Azure Resources and the deployment of code, must be scripted. No ad hoc system administration CAN take place in any environment beyond the Development environment. The scripts must be constructed and tested in the Development environment.

requirement.name: All Azure resources defined in Bicep, deployed as an Azure Deployment Stack
requirement.requirement: Every Azure resource backing the Pipeline (Flex Consumption Function App, App Service Plan, Storage Account for AzureWebJobsStorage + NPPES blobs, Application Insights workspace, Managed Identity role assignments, Cost Management budget, Activity Log alert rules) MUST be declared in a Bicep template under infra/pipeline/ and deployed via an Azure Deployment Stack at subscription scope ('az stack sub create'). No resource may be created or modified by 'az functionapp create', portal click, or stand-alone 'az deployment'. Verification: a CI job runs 'az stack sub show --name pipeline-{env} --query resources[].id -o tsv' and a separate 'az resource list --resource-group rg-pipeline-{env} --query [].id -o tsv'; the diff MUST be empty (every resource in the RG is a managed resource of the stack).

requirement.name: Deployment Stack denyWriteAndDelete blocks portal/CLI changes in QA and Prod
requirement.requirement: The Azure Deployment Stack for QA and Prod MUST be created with --deny-settings-mode denyWriteAndDelete --deny-settings-apply-to-child-scopes per Microsoft Learn 'Protect managed resources'. The deny-assignment MUST exclude only the deploy-pipeline OIDC service principal (--deny-settings-excluded-principals <ci-sp-object-id>). The Development environment stack MAY use --deny-settings-mode none to permit ad-hoc operator work. Verification: an automated check runs 'az role assignment list --include-deny-assignments --scope <rg-id>' against QA and Prod monthly and asserts a denyWriteAndDelete assignment exists whose excluded principals list contains exactly the CI service principal. Known limitation acknowledged: deny-settings cover the control plane only; data-plane operations (writes inside a storage container, secrets in Key Vault) are not covered — those are handled by REQ-T-004.

requirement.name: GitHub Actions deploys via Microsoft Entra federated OIDC, no long-lived secrets
requirement.requirement: The GitHub Actions workflow that deploys the Bicep stack and Function App code MUST authenticate to Azure exclusively via OpenID Connect federated identity credentials on a Microsoft Entra application or user-assigned Managed Identity (per Microsoft Learn 'Deploy Bicep files by using GitHub Actions'). No AZURE_CREDENTIALS JSON service-principal secret MAY be stored in GitHub repository or environment secrets for QA or Prod. The workflow MUST use 'permissions: id-token: write' and 'azure/login@v2' with client-id, tenant-id, subscription-id only. Verification: a CI lint step parses every workflow YAML under .github/workflows/deploy-pipelines*.yml, asserts 'id-token: write' is set, and asserts the azure/login step does NOT carry a 'creds:' parameter. (Today's deploy-pipelines.yml uses 'creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}' — this REQ-T mandates the migration.)

requirement.name: Azure Monitor activity-log alert detects ad-hoc writes outside the deploy pipeline
requirement.requirement: An Azure Monitor activity-log alert rule MUST exist on each QA and Prod resource group covering operation names Microsoft.Web/sites/*/write, Microsoft.Web/sites/*/delete, Microsoft.App/jobs/*/write, Microsoft.App/jobs/*/delete, Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/write, and Microsoft.Insights/components/write. The alert MUST fire whenever the caller's claims.appid is NOT the deploy-pipeline OIDC service principal client ID. The action group MUST route the alert through the existing pipeline_health.send_admin_notification SparkPost path so Skip is notified within Microsoft Learn's stated 3-20 minute Activity Log latency window. Verification: a synthetic test in dev triggers a portal-style write (e.g. tag change) using a non-CI principal and asserts an email arrives within 30 minutes.

depends_on.reason: Closes the data-plane gap left by REQ-T-002 and depends on REQ-T-003's pipeline service principal identity.

requirement.name: Scripts proven against Development Deployment Stack before promotion
requirement.requirement: Every change to infra/pipeline/main.bicep (or any module it imports) MUST be applied to the Development Deployment Stack via 'az stack sub create --deployment-resource-group rg-pipeline-dev' AND a 'az deployment sub what-if' MUST be attached to the Pull Request before merge to dev. The promotion-to-qa GitHub Actions workflow MUST refuse to run against QA if the same git SHA has not previously been recorded as having succeeded against dev (a deployments collection in the front-end MongoDB cluster, written by the dev workflow, serves as the lookup). Verification: the QA deploy job's first step queries that collection by SHA and exits non-zero on miss. Aligns with REQ-B-002's last sentence that scripts must be constructed and tested in Development.

depends_on.reason: Depends on the Bicep + stack baseline (REQ-T-001) and the OIDC pipeline (REQ-T-003).

story.name: Compute runtime — every pipeline runs on the Pipeline Function App
story.description: All Pipeline orchestrators run as Durable Functions on a single shared Azure Functions Flex Consumption Function App per environment. The runtime, the orchestration timeout, the instance ceiling, and the per-instance memory size are universal — every pipeline inherits them; no pipeline is permitted its own Function App or its own runtime configuration.

requirement.name: Every pipeline orchestrator runs on the single Pipeline Function App
requirement.requirement: Every Pipeline orchestrator MUST be a Durable Functions orchestrator deployed to the one Pipeline Function App per environment. Pipelines MUST NOT spin up their own Function App, their own Container Apps Job, or any other compute host. The Pipeline Function App is the only compute target that satisfies REQ-B-001's horizontal-scale, 2-hour, and zero-idle constraints together.

requirement.name: Function App runtime is Azure Functions Flex Consumption (Linux, Python)
requirement.requirement: The Pipeline Function App runtime MUST be Azure Functions Flex Consumption on Linux with Python. This is the only runtime evaluated against REQ-B-001's zero-idle-cost rule (Microsoft Learn: Flex Consumption scales to zero with no minimum-instance billing when alwaysReady is empty).

requirement.name: host.json functionTimeout = 02:00:00 enforces REQ-B-001's 2-hour ceiling
requirement.requirement: host.json on the Pipeline Function App MUST set functionTimeout to 02:00:00. This is the platform-enforced upper bound on a single orchestration; the platform cancels orchestrations that exceed it. No pipeline may relax or override this value.

requirement.name: scaleAndConcurrency.maximumInstanceCount is the universal fan-out ceiling
requirement.requirement: The Pipeline Function App MUST have scaleAndConcurrency.maximumInstanceCount set to a documented value per environment. This value is the hard ceiling on simultaneous worker activities across every pipeline's fan-out. F-029 mandates that the cap is set; the per-environment value is a deployment artifact.

requirement.name: scaleAndConcurrency.instanceMemoryMB sized for partition processing
requirement.requirement: The Pipeline Function App MUST have scaleAndConcurrency.instanceMemoryMB set to a value sized for the largest single-partition working set that any pipeline activity will process. F-029 mandates that the value is set explicitly; the per-environment number is a deployment artifact justified by partition-size analysis.

story.name: Cluster reservation contract — every pipeline calls the DB manager
story.description: The Mongo Pipeline cluster is reserved through one and only one mechanism: the register_reservation_activity / release_reservation_activity pair on the Pipeline Function App, which delegate to ClusterLifecycleManager. No pipeline, no ops tool, no human session is permitted to bypass that pair when intending to use the cluster.

requirement.name: register_reservation_activity and release_reservation_activity are the only path to reserve the Mongo Pipeline cluster
requirement.requirement: Every pipeline orchestrator MUST call register_reservation_activity at start (before any work that touches the Mongo Pipeline cluster) and release_reservation_activity in a finally block (after the orchestration completes, succeeds, or fails). These two Durable Functions activities, registered on the Pipeline Function App, are the only sanctioned path to acquire or release the cluster. No pipeline may call ClusterLifecycleManager directly; no pipeline may issue Atlas Admin API calls of its own.

requirement.name: register_reservation_activity arg semantics — universal contract across every pipeline
requirement.requirement: register_reservation_activity accepts a single dict argument with these fields, which every pipeline MUST populate: job_id (string, MUST equal the orchestration instance_id, used as the unique reservation key); requester (string, MUST identify the calling pipeline by name); cluster_name (string, the name of the Mongo Pipeline cluster the reservation targets); expected_duration_minutes (integer, the maximum wall-clock budget the pipeline reserves before being deemed overdue); reservation_class (string, 'automated' for any pipeline orchestrator and 'user' for any human-driven session). Any pipeline that omits any of these fields, or passes values that violate these semantics, has not made a valid reservation.

requirement.name: Sub-orchestrators MUST NOT register or release; only the parent orchestrator holds the reservation
requirement.requirement: When a pipeline is composed of a parent orchestrator and one or more sub-orchestrators, only the parent orchestrator MUST register the reservation at the very start and release it in finally. Sub-orchestrators MUST NOT call register_reservation_activity or release_reservation_activity. This rule prevents nested reservations and double-release races.

requirement.name: Non-orchestrator callers MUST register as reservation_class='user'
requirement.requirement: Any caller that is not a pipeline orchestrator (interactive CLI, ops tool, UI session, ad-hoc admin task) wishing to use the Mongo Pipeline cluster MUST register a reservation with reservation_class='user'. The 'user' class is the single signal the pause gate uses to suppress auto-pause while a human is actively connected (REQ-B-002's User-reservation carve-out).

story.name: Pre-warm and cool-down — the only permitted scaling mechanism
story.description: Every pipeline that fans out worker activities MUST pre-warm Function App instances before fan-out and cool them down after. The mechanism is the same for every pipeline: an ARM PATCH to scaleAndConcurrency.alwaysReady on the Pipeline Function App, authenticated via Service Principal client_credentials OAuth, with a propagation wait derived from observed PATCH latency.

requirement.name: Every fan-out pipeline MUST PATCH alwaysReady to a non-empty list before fan-out
requirement.requirement: Every pipeline that fans out worker activities MUST PATCH the Pipeline Function App's properties.functionAppConfig.scaleAndConcurrency.alwaysReady to [{name: 'durable', instanceCount: <pipeline-specified>}] via the Azure Resource Manager API before fan-out begins. The instanceCount value is per-pipeline (set by the calling pipeline based on its planned partition count); F-029 mandates that the value MUST be set — pipelines may not rely on cold-start. The 'name' field MUST be 'durable' (the per-function scale group containing all Durable Functions triggers per Microsoft Learn 'Per-function scaling'); it MUST NOT be a named-function value.

requirement.name: Auth for the alwaysReady PATCH is Service Principal client_credentials OAuth — no MSI
requirement.requirement: The PATCH MUST be authenticated using a dedicated Pipeline Service Principal via the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant against https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token, with scope https://management.azure.com/.default. The SP env-var contract is universal: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_PIPELINE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_PIPELINE_CLIENT_SECRET (token), plus AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID and AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP (target). The SP MUST hold Website Contributor on the Function App resource. IMDS-based Managed Identity is NOT permitted — IMDS (169.254.169.254) is unreachable from Flex Consumption Python activity workers and silently fails; SP OAuth is the only sanctioned auth path.

requirement.name: Propagation wait is 3 x ack_latency, floored at 60 seconds
requirement.requirement: After the PATCH returns 200, the orchestrator MUST wait at least 3 x the observed ack latency, with a hard floor of 60 seconds, before releasing fan-out. This prevents the two-wave cold-start pattern that occurs when fan-out is released before alwaysReady propagation completes. The wait is enforced inside warm_instances_fn before returning.

requirement.name: Cool-down: PATCH alwaysReady back to [] after fan-out completes
requirement.requirement: After fan-out completes (whether the run succeeded or failed), the orchestrator MUST PATCH alwaysReady back to [] using the same SP-OAuth path. This realizes REQ-B-001's zero-idle-cost rule on the Function App side: with alwaysReady empty, the platform scales the app to zero instances when no executions are running.

requirement.name: Pre-warm and cool-down operations record metrics to a shared collection
requirement.requirement: Every pre-warm and cool-down operation MUST record timestamps and the observed ack latency to a single shared Mongo collection on the Mongo Pipeline cluster, so that propagation behavior is observable across pipelines without per-pipeline metrics infrastructure. The collection is named per a documented infrastructure convention; F-029 mandates that the metrics are written, not the per-environment collection name.

story.name: Idle posture and Mongo Pipeline cluster auto-pause
story.description: Realizes REQ-B-002 (auto-pause unless User reservation) and the zero-idle-cost half of REQ-B-001. Between Pipeline runs the system MUST hold the Function App with alwaysReady empty and the Mongo Pipeline cluster paused. A 5-minute timer-driven reaper enforces the policy by deleting overdue automated reservations and pausing the cluster when no live reservations remain. User-class reservations are exempt — they age out only when the user releases.

requirement.name: Between runs: Function App alwaysReady = [] (cool-down enforced)
requirement.requirement: Between Pipeline runs the Pipeline Function App MUST hold scaleAndConcurrency.alwaysReady = [] (the empty list). This is enforced by S-005's cool-down step at the end of every fan-out. F-029 mandates the steady-state value, not a transient one.

requirement.name: 5-minute Azure Functions timer trigger drives the cluster reaper
requirement.requirement: An Azure Functions timer trigger MUST run on the Pipeline Function App on a 5-minute schedule. Its responsibility is to read the live reservation document from the DB manager, identify overdue automated reservations, delete them, and — when no live reservations remain — pause the Mongo Pipeline cluster via the Mongo Atlas Admin API. The timer MUST NOT execute pipeline business logic and MUST NOT register reservations of its own.

requirement.name: Reaper deletes overdue automated reservations; deletion is the only state change
requirement.requirement: The reaper MUST delete reservation rows where (now > expected_end_time + GRACE_MINUTES) AND (reservation_class == 'automated'). Deletion is the only sanctioned state change — the reaper MUST NOT transition rows to a status='orphan' value, MUST NOT preserve overdue rows in any form, and MUST NOT write a release_time field. The reservation collection is live-only by REQ-T-007 below.

requirement.name: User-class reservations MUST NOT age out
requirement.requirement: Reservation rows where reservation_class == 'user' MUST NOT be subject to the overdue check or the reaper's deletion. They are released only when the user explicitly releases via release_reservation_activity. This realizes REQ-B-002's User-reservation carve-out: the cluster stays unpaused for as long as a User reservation is present.

requirement.name: GRACE_MINUTES = 30 is the universal overdue tolerance for automated reservations
requirement.requirement: The grace window beyond expected_end_time before an automated reservation is treated as overdue MUST be 30 minutes. This is a single value applied universally — pipelines may not opt for a longer or shorter grace. The 30-minute value is justified by observed worst-case retry/back-off intervals; changing it is a F-029 amendment, not a per-pipeline tunable.

requirement.name: When zero live reservations remain, the DB manager MUST pause the cluster via the Mongo Atlas Admin API
requirement.requirement: When the reaper observes zero live reservations on the Mongo Pipeline cluster, it MUST issue a pause request to the Mongo Atlas Admin API for that cluster (the only sanctioned path for pause/resume). The pause MUST proceed regardless of which class of reservation last released (automated reaping or user release). This realizes REQ-B-002's primary outcome and the cost-side of REQ-B-001.

requirement.name: Reservation collection is live-only — no history, no TTL, no released/orphan persisted state
requirement.requirement: The reservation collection on the Mongo Pipeline cluster MUST hold only currently-live reservations. release_reservation_activity MUST delete the released row; it MUST NOT transition a status field, MUST NOT write a release_time history field, and MUST NOT preserve the row. The collection MUST NOT carry a TTL index for reservation history because no history is retained. Forensic and audit needs are satisfied by S-008's external sinks.

story.name: Cost guard — Azure Cost Management budget with action-group alerting
story.description: A defensive backstop for REQ-B-001's zero-idle-cost rule: if the auto-pause + cool-down mechanisms ever fail silently, an Azure Cost Management budget tripwire fires before the bill grows materially.

requirement.name: Azure Cost Management budget exists at subscription scope, scoped by workload tag
requirement.requirement: An Azure Cost Management budget MUST exist on the Pipeline subscription, scoped by a workload tag so that storage costs (which REQ-B-001 explicitly exempts) are excluded from the cap. The budget amount per period is a per-environment deployment artifact; F-029 mandates that the budget exists and is wired.

requirement.name: Two threshold rules fire to an action group that calls send_admin_notification
requirement.requirement: The budget MUST have at least two threshold rules (e.g. 50% and 90% of budget) wired to an Azure Monitor Action Group. The action group MUST trigger pipeline_health.send_admin_notification (SparkPost) so admin email is the operational tripwire. Webhook-only or email-only configurations that bypass the existing notification function are NOT compliant.

story.name: Forensic audit sinks — three external sinks replacing in-app history
story.description: Because the reservation collection is live-only (S-006-REQ-T-007), forensic and audit capability MUST come from external platform sinks. Three sinks together cover every audit need that an in-application history table would have served.

requirement.name: Mongo Atlas database auditing enabled on the Pipeline cluster's project
requirement.requirement: Mongo Atlas database auditing MUST be enabled on the Atlas project that hosts the Mongo Pipeline cluster, so that every write and delete against the reservation collection (and every other collection in the cluster) lands in Atlas's native audit log with strictly-append-only retention controlled by Atlas.

requirement.name: Function App diagnostic settings ship to Application Insights and Log Analytics
requirement.requirement: The Pipeline Function App MUST have diagnostic settings configured to ship request and trace logs to an Application Insights resource and an Azure Monitor Log Analytics workspace. These two sinks are the canonical place to investigate orchestrator behavior, activity invocations, and SP-OAuth failures.

requirement.name: Azure Activity Log on the Pipeline subscription captures every control-plane operation
requirement.requirement: Azure Activity Log MUST be enabled at subscription scope and routed to the same Log Analytics workspace used by the Function App diagnostic settings. Activity Log captures every control-plane operation (resource changes, ARM PATCHes, deployment-stack actions) against the Pipeline subscription, completing the three-sink audit picture.

story.description: When the last reservation is released, ClusterLifecycleManager.release must send a pause request to Atlas. This is the single place that decides when to pause — no orchestrator should pause directly.

requirement.requirement: A developer must be able to manually create a reservation (to keep the cluster alive for debugging) and manually remove it (to let the cluster pause).
requirement.name: Manually create and remove cluster reservations for debugging purposes

requirement.requirement: When release removes the last reservation for a cluster, it must call _send_pause(cluster_name). Boolean test: release last reservation → Atlas API receives PATCH {paused: true}.
requirement.name: release triggers _send_pause when last cluster reservation is removed

requirement.requirement: No orchestrator may call _send_pause or pause_cluster directly. Only ClusterLifecycleManager.release and force_release_all may pause. Boolean test: grep all orchestrator functions for 'pause' → zero matches.
requirement.name: Restrict pause calls to ClusterLifecycleManager.release and force_release_all

requirement.requirement: The timer (every 30 seconds) must check for zero reservations. If zero reservations and cluster is IDLE, pause the cluster. This is the auto-shutdown mechanism.
requirement.name: Timer pauses IDLE cluster with zero reservations every 30 seconds (auto-shutdown

requirement.requirement: Failsafe: if the cluster is paused, any remaining reservations must be automatically removed. A paused cluster cannot have active reservations.
requirement.name: Auto-remove reservations when cluster is paused; enforce no active reservations

story.name: ClusterLifecycleManager.release must auto-pause when zero reservations remain

story.description: reserve calls time.sleep in a loop for up to 10 minutes inside a Durable Functions activity. Activities must complete quickly. Wake and poll must be separated: reserve sends wake + registers reservation and returns immediately. The orchestrator polls via check_cluster_state_activity + create_timer.

requirement.requirement: ClusterLifecycleManager.reserve must NOT call time.sleep. It must send the wake request and register the reservation, then return immediately. Boolean test: reserve completes in under 5 seconds.
requirement.name: reserve must not sleep; send wake, register, and return within 5 seconds

requirement.name: Reserving orchestrators must call check_cluster_state_activity after register
